grammar.key: TIME (soon, see you soon, get well soon)
grammar.en: Use soon in farewell and recovery wishes.
grammar.desc: soon을 작별 인사와 쾌유 기원에 사용함
examples: See you soon.

grammar.key: DEGREE WITH VERBS (really, very much, like, love)
grammar.en: Intensify liking with really or very much.
grammar.desc: really와 very much로 선호의 강도를 강조함
examples: I really like this soup.

grammar.en: Describe frequency with always and sometimes.
grammar.desc: always와 sometimes로 행동 빈도를 나타냄
examples: I sometimes walk to school.

grammar.en: Make affirmative statements with can.
grammar.desc: can으로 능력을 긍정 서술함
examples: I can swim.

grammar.en: Place can before the subject in questions.
grammar.desc: can을 주어 앞에 놓아 의문문을 만듦
examples: Can you swim?

grammar.en: Negate can with cannot or can't.
grammar.desc: cannot과 can't로 능력을 부정함
examples: I cannot swim.

grammar.en: Join common adjectives with and.
grammar.desc: and로 기본 형용사를 연결함
examples: The room is warm and bright.

grammar.key: MAIN CLAUSE + MAIN CLAUSE (and, but, or)
grammar.en: Connect complete statements with and, but or or.
grammar.desc: and·but·or로 완전한 서술절을 연결함
examples: I like tea, but my sister likes coffee.

grammar.en: Omit a repeated subject in the second clause.
grammar.desc: 두 번째 절에서 반복되는 주어를 생략함
examples: I washed the cups and put them away.

grammar.en: State an intention with will or 'll.
grammar.desc: will과 'll로 계획과 의도를 나타냄
examples: I'll call you tonight.

grammar.en: Build affirmative clauses with will.
grammar.desc: will을 사용한 긍정절을 만듦
examples: I will bring the books.

grammar.en: Invert be and the subject to ask a question.
grammar.desc: be동사와 주어의 순서를 바꾸어 질문함
examples: Are you ready?

grammar.en: Put really between the subject and main verb.
grammar.desc: 주어와 본동사 사이에 really를 놓아 강조함
examples: I really enjoy cooking.

grammar.key: WITH NOUNS (my, your, his, her, our)
grammar.en: Put possessive determiners before nouns.
grammar.desc: 명사 앞에 소유 한정사를 사용함
examples: This is our house.

grammar.key: WITH PLURAL NOUNS (some, lots of, a lot of)
grammar.en: Quantify plural nouns with some or a lot of.
grammar.desc: some과 a lot of 등으로 복수 명사의 수량을 나타냄
examples: We have some apples.

grammar.en: Use a and every before singular nouns.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사 앞에 a와 every를 사용함
examples: Every student has a pencil.

grammar.en: Give a reason in a because clause after a statement.
grammar.desc: 서술절 뒤 because절로 이유를 제시함
examples: I stayed home because I was ill.

grammar.en: Introduce a reason clause with because.
grammar.desc: because로 이유를 나타내는 종속절을 이끎
examples: We left early because it was raining.

grammar.key: MY BEST FRIEND (my best friend, best)
grammar.en: Use best in the phrase my best friend.
grammar.desc: my best friend에서 불규칙 최상급 best를 사용함
examples: Maya is my best friend.

grammar.en: Form affirmative future clauses with will.
grammar.desc: will로 긍정 미래절을 구성함
examples: The bus will arrive soon.

grammar.en: Use would like in affirmative clauses.
grammar.desc: would like를 긍정절에 사용하여 희망을 나타냄
examples: I would like a cup of tea.

grammar.key: INVITATIONS WITH LIKE (would, wouldn't, like, would like to invite)
grammar.en: Invite someone with would like to invite.
grammar.desc: would like to invite로 상대방을 초대함
examples: I would like to invite you to dinner.

grammar.en: Use this with a forthcoming time or date.
grammar.desc: 다가오는 시간이나 날짜에 this를 사용함
examples: I'm meeting her this Friday.

grammar.en: Use everything as a singular subject.
grammar.desc: everything을 단수 주어로 사용함
examples: Everything looks clean.

grammar.en: Use can't before a base-form verb.
grammar.desc: 동사 원형 앞에 can't를 사용하여 부정함
examples: I can't drive.

grammar.en: Negate present-simple verbs with don't.
grammar.desc: don't와 동사 원형으로 현재형을 부정함
examples: I don't eat meat.

grammar.en: Use regular and irregular past-simple forms.
grammar.desc: 규칙·불규칙 과거형으로 긍정문을 구성함
examples: I visited my aunt yesterday.

grammar.en: Describe everyday past events and states.
grammar.desc: 일상의 과거 사건과 상태를 단순과거로 서술함
examples: We cooked dinner last night.

grammar.en: Follow like with an infinitive or an -ing form.
grammar.desc: like 뒤에 to부정사나 동명사를 사용함
examples: I like reading in the evening.

grammar.en: Follow would like with a to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: would like 뒤 to부정사로 희망을 나타냄
examples: I would like to visit Rome.

grammar.en: Use really to intensify a present-simple statement.
grammar.desc: really로 현재형 서술의 의미를 강조함
examples: I really like this song.

grammar.en: Form negative present-simple clauses.
grammar.desc: 기본 동사를 사용하여 현재형 부정절을 만듦
examples: I don't work on Sundays.

grammar.en: Use the present simple for habits and facts.
grammar.desc: 현재형으로 습관과 일반적인 사실을 나타냄
examples: Water freezes at zero degrees.

grammar.en: Use you or it after be in questions.
grammar.desc: be동사 의문문에서 you와 it을 주어로 사용함
examples: Are you tired?

grammar.key: (OBJECT) WITH PREPOSITION (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
grammar.en: Use object pronouns after prepositions.
grammar.desc: 전치사 뒤에 목적격 인칭대명사를 사용함
examples: Please sit beside me.

grammar.en: Put personal pronouns after question auxiliaries.
grammar.desc: 의문문에서 조동사 뒤에 인칭대명사를 사용함
examples: Do they live nearby?

grammar.key: (OBJECT) ME, YOU, HER, HIM, US, THEM (me, you, her, him, us, them)
grammar.en: Use object pronouns after transitive verbs.
grammar.desc: 타동사 뒤 직접목적어에 목적격 대명사를 사용함
examples: I saw him yesterday.

grammar.en: Describe a singular entity with there is.
grammar.desc: there is와 단수 명사로 존재를 나타냄
examples: There is a chair by the window.

grammar.en: Describe plural entities with there are.
grammar.desc: there are와 복수 명사로 존재를 나타냄
examples: There are two chairs by the window.

grammar.en: Use can, will and would before a main verb.
grammar.desc: 본동사 앞에 can·will·would를 사용함
examples: I can help you today.

grammar.key: WISHES AND PREFERENCES WITH LIKE (would, wouldn't, like, would like)
grammar.en: Express wishes and preferences with would like.
grammar.desc: would like로 희망과 선호를 나타냄
examples: I would like a quieter room.

grammar.en: Form yes-no questions with a modal verb first.
grammar.desc: 문두 조동사로 예·아니요 의문문을 구성함
examples: Can we start now?

grammar.en: State certainty with I am sure and a clause.
grammar.desc: I am sure 뒤 절로 확신하는 내용을 제시함
examples: I'm sure the shop is open.

grammar.en: Mark an attitude with actually or unfortunately.
grammar.desc: actually와 unfortunately 등으로 태도를 나타냄
examples: Unfortunately, the train is late.

grammar.en: Link ideas with also, so and however.
grammar.desc: also·so·however로 문장 간 관계를 나타냄
examples: It was raining; however, we went outside.

grammar.en: Order discourse with first, then and after that.
grammar.desc: first·then·after that으로 발화의 순서를 나타냄
examples: First, wash the rice. Then, add water.

grammar.en: Qualify certainty with maybe or perhaps.
grammar.desc: maybe와 perhaps로 확실성의 정도를 나타냄
examples: Perhaps she is at home.

grammar.en: Locate an event in time with common adverbs.
grammar.desc: 시간 부사로 사건이 일어나는 시점을 나타냄
examples: I finished the task yesterday.

grammar.en: Describe frequency with usually, often or never.
grammar.desc: usually·often·never 등으로 빈도를 나타냄
examples: We usually eat at six.

grammar.key: DEGREE WITH VERBS (so much, a lot)
grammar.en: Modify verbs with so much or a lot.
grammar.desc: so much와 a lot으로 동작의 정도를 나타냄
examples: I miss you so much.

grammar.key: COMBINING TWO ADJECTIVES WITH BUT (but, be)
grammar.en: Contrast two adjectives after be with but.
grammar.desc: be동사 뒤 형용사 두 개를 but으로 대조함
examples: The room is small but comfortable.

grammar.en: Use more to compare longer adjectives.
grammar.desc: 긴 형용사 앞에 more를 사용하여 비교함
examples: This chair is more comfortable.

grammar.en: Use irregular comparative adjective forms.
grammar.desc: 불규칙 형용사 비교급을 사용함
examples: This route is better.

grammar.en: Add -r to one-syllable adjectives ending in e.
grammar.desc: e로 끝나는 단음절 형용사에 r을 붙여 비교함
examples: The new hall is larger.

grammar.en: Place comparative adjectives before nouns.
grammar.desc: 명사 앞에 비교급 형용사를 사용하여 수식함
examples: We need a larger table.

grammar.en: Use a comparative adjective after be.
grammar.desc: be동사 뒤에 비교급 형용사를 사용함
examples: This bag is heavier.

grammar.en: Double the final consonant before comparative -er.
grammar.desc: 단모음 뒤 끝자음을 겹치고 er을 붙여 비교함
examples: This box is bigger.

grammar.en: Change final y to i before comparative -er.
grammar.desc: 끝의 y를 i로 바꾸고 er을 붙여 비교함
examples: This street is busier.

grammar.en: Add -er to common one-syllable adjectives.
grammar.desc: 기본 단음절 형용사에 er을 붙여 비교함
examples: This ruler is longer.

grammar.key: BE LIKE + NOUN OR PRONOUN (be like, be, like)
grammar.en: Express resemblance with be like and a noun.
grammar.desc: be like 뒤 명사나 대명사로 유사성을 나타냄
examples: The cloud is like a sheep.

grammar.en: Compare two noun phrases with adjective plus than.
grammar.desc: 비교급 형용사와 than으로 두 대상을 비교함
examples: This box is smaller than that one.

grammar.en: Join ordered instruction clauses with conjunctions.
grammar.desc: 접속사와 쉼표로 순차적인 지시절을 연결함
examples: Turn left, cross the road, and enter the station.

grammar.en: Use these before plural nouns.
grammar.desc: 복수 명사 앞에 these를 사용함
examples: These shoes are new.

grammar.en: Use those before plural nouns.
grammar.desc: 복수 명사 앞에 those를 사용함
examples: Those trees are tall.

grammar.en: Point to more distant things with those.
grammar.desc: those로 시간·공간상 멀리 있는 대상을 가리킴
examples: Look at those mountains over there.

grammar.en: Refer back to mentioned things with those.
grammar.desc: those로 앞서 언급한 대상을 다시 가리킴
examples: I bought two books yesterday. Those were expensive.

grammar.en: Refer to relevant or mentioned things with these.
grammar.desc: these로 관련성이 높은 대상을 다시 가리킴
examples: We have two problems. These need attention.

grammar.en: Point to things near the speaker with these.
grammar.desc: these로 화자 관점에서 가까운 대상을 가리킴
examples: These are the keys in my hand.

grammar.key: WILL BE ABLE TO (will be able to, will, be able to)
grammar.en: Describe future ability with will be able to.
grammar.desc: will be able to로 미래의 능력과 가능성을 나타냄
examples: I will be able to drive next year.

grammar.en: Describe an ongoing future event with will be -ing.
grammar.desc: 미래진행형으로 특정 미래 시점의 동작을 나타냄
examples: At eight tomorrow, I'll be travelling to London.

grammar.en: Build affirmative future-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: will be와 동사 ing형으로 긍정 미래진행절을 만듦
examples: It will be raining tomorrow morning.

grammar.en: Use shall in affirmative clauses with I or we.
grammar.desc: I와 we를 주어로 shall 긍정절을 구성함
examples: I shall call you tomorrow.

grammar.en: Offer assistance with Shall I.
grammar.desc: Shall I로 도움을 제안함
examples: Shall I carry your bag?

grammar.en: Form future negatives with will not or won't.
grammar.desc: will not과 won't로 미래 부정문을 만듦
examples: I won't be late.

grammar.en: Ask future questions with will or shall.
grammar.desc: will과 shall로 미래 관련 질문을 구성함
examples: Will the bus stop here?

grammar.en: Request an action with will in a question.
grammar.desc: will 의문문으로 상대방의 행동을 요청함
examples: Will you close the door, please?

grammar.en: Express willingness to act with will.
grammar.desc: will로 행동하려는 자발적인 의사를 나타냄
examples: I will help you carry the boxes.

grammar.en: Suggest a shared action with Shall we.
grammar.desc: Shall we로 함께할 행동을 제안함
examples: Shall we eat outside?

grammar.en: Ask about intentions using will.
grammar.desc: will 의문문으로 계획과 의도를 질문함
examples: Will you visit your family this weekend?

grammar.en: Ask about plans with be going to.
grammar.desc: be going to 의문문으로 계획을 질문함
examples: Are you going to leave tomorrow?

grammar.en: State future intentions with be going to.
grammar.desc: be going to 긍정문으로 앞으로의 의도를 나타냄
examples: I'm going to study tonight.

grammar.key: AFFIRMATIVE (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Use affirmative have to and have got to forms.
grammar.desc: have to와 have got to 긍정형으로 필요를 나타냄
examples: She has to wear a uniform.

grammar.key: QUESTIONS (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Ask about necessity with have to.
grammar.desc: have to 의문문으로 필요한 행동을 질문함
examples: Do we have to book a table?

grammar.key: NEGATIVE (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Express lack of necessity with don't have to.
grammar.desc: don't have to로 행동할 필요가 없음을 나타냄
examples: You don't have to pay today.

grammar.key: OBLIGATION (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to) (A3)
grammar.en: Express obligations with have to or have got to.
grammar.desc: have to와 have got to로 의무를 나타냄
examples: I've got to finish this report.
grammar.surface: OBLIGATION (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)

grammar.en: Reinforce an instruction with a negative imperative.
grammar.desc: 지시 뒤 부정 명령문을 덧붙여 주의를 강조함
examples: Turn off the cooker. Don't forget.

grammar.en: Give instructions with a base-form imperative.
grammar.desc: 동사 원형 명령문으로 행동을 지시함
examples: Press the green button.

grammar.en: Suggest a shared action with let's and a verb.
grammar.desc: let's 뒤 동사 원형으로 함께할 행동을 제안함
examples: Let's take a break.

grammar.en: Ask yes-no questions with auxiliary do.
grammar.desc: 조동사 do로 일반동사 의문문을 구성함
examples: Do you like this song?

grammar.en: Ask about an object with a wh-word.
grammar.desc: 의문사로 목적어에 해당하는 정보를 질문함
examples: What did you buy?

grammar.key: AFFIRMATIVE INTERROGATIVE, WITH AUXILIARY BE/HAVE (be, have)
grammar.en: Ask yes-no questions with auxiliary be or have.
grammar.desc: 조동사 be와 have로 의문문을 구성함
examples: Have you finished dinner?

grammar.en: Build questions with a negative auxiliary.
grammar.desc: 부정형 조동사로 부정 의문문을 구성함
examples: Didn't you see the sign?

grammar.en: Combine a wh-word with a negative question.
grammar.desc: 의문사와 부정형을 결합하여 의문문을 구성함
examples: Why didn't you call me?

grammar.key: AFFIRMATIVE INTERROGATIVE, WITH MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
grammar.en: Ask yes-no questions with modal auxiliaries.
grammar.desc: 법조동사로 예·아니요 의문문을 구성함
examples: Can you open the window?

grammar.en: Use may in an affirmative clause.
grammar.desc: may를 사용한 긍정절을 구성함
examples: The parcel may arrive today.

grammar.en: Use might to express a possible event.
grammar.desc: might로 일어날 수 있는 사건을 나타냄
examples: She might visit tomorrow.

grammar.en: Grade adjectives with really, so and quite.
grammar.desc: really·so·quite로 형용사의 정도를 나타냄
examples: The water is quite cold.

grammar.en: Build affirmative clauses with must.
grammar.desc: must 긍정절로 의무 등을 나타냄
examples: You must wear a seat belt.

grammar.en: Express prohibition with must not or mustn't.
grammar.desc: must not과 mustn't로 금지를 나타냄
examples: You mustn't park here.

grammar.key: WOULD LOVE + TO (would love, to, would love to)
grammar.en: Express a strong wish with would love to.
grammar.desc: would love to 뒤 동사 원형으로 강한 희망을 나타냄
examples: I would love to visit Canada.

grammar.en: Use look forward to before a noun or -ing form.
grammar.desc: look forward to 뒤 명사나 동명사로 기대를 나타냄
examples: I look forward to meeting you.

grammar.key: WHAT A PITY + (THAT) CLAUSE (what a pity, that)
grammar.en: Express regret with What a pity and a clause.
grammar.desc: What a pity 뒤 절로 유감의 내용을 나타냄
examples: What a pity that you can't come.

grammar.en: Build an exclamation with What a and a noun.
grammar.desc: What a 뒤 명사구로 감탄문을 구성함
examples: What a lovely garden!

grammar.en: Describe appearance or feeling with a linking verb.
grammar.desc: look과 feel 뒤 형용사로 외양과 느낌을 나타냄
examples: You look tired.

grammar.en: Limit a noun's reference with main or only.
grammar.desc: main과 only로 명사가 가리키는 범위를 한정함
examples: This is the main entrance.

grammar.en: Mark possession with singular noun plus 's.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사나 고유명사 뒤 's로 소유를 나타냄
examples: This is Emma's coat.

grammar.en: Use present simple after when for future time.
grammar.desc: 미래 시간의 when절에 현재형을 사용함
examples: I'll call you when I arrive.

grammar.en: Ask about arrangements in the present continuous.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형 의문문으로 앞으로의 일정을 질문함
examples: Are you meeting Sam tomorrow?

grammar.en: Use present simple for future timetables.
grammar.desc: 현재형으로 시간표에 정해진 미래 일정을 나타냄
examples: The train leaves at nine tomorrow.

grammar.en: Use present continuous for future arrangements.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형으로 확정한 미래 일정을 나타냄
examples: I'm meeting Sam tomorrow.

grammar.key: WITH PLURAL NOUNS (all, both, a few)
grammar.en: Quantify plural nouns with all, both or a few.
grammar.desc: all·both·a few로 복수 명사의 수량을 나타냄
examples: Both students have tickets.

grammar.key: DETERMINER + OF + DETERMINER (of, all of, some of, both of, many of, any of, each of)
grammar.en: Place of between a quantifier and determiner.
grammar.desc: 수량 한정사와 한정사 사이에 of를 사용함
examples: Some of the students are waiting outside.

grammar.key: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS (some, any, no, more, a lot of)
grammar.en: Quantify plural and uncountable nouns.
grammar.desc: 수량 한정사로 복수·불가산 명사를 한정함
examples: We need more chairs and more water.

grammar.en: Use many before plural nouns in negatives.
grammar.desc: 부정문에서 복수 명사 앞에 many를 사용함
examples: I don't have many books.

grammar.en: Use much before uncountable nouns in negatives.
grammar.desc: 부정문에서 불가산 명사 앞에 much를 사용함
examples: I don't have much time.

grammar.en: Use each, an and one before singular nouns.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사 앞에 each·an·one을 사용함
examples: Each child has a ticket.

grammar.key: SO MANY WITH PLURAL NOUNS (so many, too many)
grammar.en: Use so many or too many with plural nouns.
grammar.desc: so many와 too many로 복수 명사의 수량을 나타냄
examples: There are too many cars here.

grammar.en: Use which as an object in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 which를 목적어로 사용함
examples: The book which I borrowed is interesting.

grammar.en: Use who as a subject in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 who를 주어로 사용함
examples: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.

grammar.en: Use that as an object in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 that을 목적어로 사용함
examples: The cake that you made is delicious.

grammar.en: Omit an object pronoun in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 목적격 관계대명사를 생략함
examples: The book I borrowed is interesting.

grammar.en: Use object which in a non-defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 비제한적 관계절에서 which를 목적어로 사용함
examples: This book, which I borrowed yesterday, is interesting.

grammar.en: Use subject which in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 which를 주어로 사용함
examples: The bus which stops here goes downtown.

grammar.en: Use subject which in a non-defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 비제한적 관계절에서 which를 주어로 사용함
examples: This bus, which stops here, goes downtown.

grammar.en: Use subject who in a non-defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 비제한적 관계절에서 who를 주어로 사용함
examples: My brother, who lives in York, is visiting.

grammar.en: Make an affirmative statement with shall.
grammar.desc: shall을 사용한 긍정 서술절을 구성함
examples: I shall return tomorrow.

grammar.en: Place shall first to ask a question.
grammar.desc: shall을 문두에 놓아 질문을 구성함
examples: Shall I wait here?

grammar.en: Use should in an affirmative statement.
grammar.desc: should를 사용한 긍정절로 권고 등을 나타냄
examples: You should take an umbrella.

grammar.en: Locate a subordinate time clause before or after a main clause.
grammar.desc: 시간 종속절을 주절 앞이나 뒤에 배치함
examples: Before we left, we locked the door.

grammar.en: Give a condition in an if clause before or after a main clause.
grammar.desc: 주절 앞이나 뒤에 if절로 조건을 제시함
examples: If it rains, we will stay home.

grammar.en: Use the most with longer superlative adjectives.
grammar.desc: 긴 형용사 앞 the most로 최상급을 나타냄
examples: This is the most comfortable chair.

grammar.en: Place maybe or perhaps before a clause.
grammar.desc: 절 앞 maybe와 perhaps로 가능성을 나타냄
examples: Maybe we can leave early.

grammar.en: Offer two same-class alternatives in an or question.
grammar.desc: or 의문문에서 같은 품사의 선택지 둘을 제시함
examples: Would you like tea or coffee?

grammar.key: PRESENT SIMPLE IF CLAUSE, REAL CONDITIONS (if, can)
grammar.en: Combine a present if clause with a real consequence.
grammar.desc: 현재형 if절로 실제 조건과 결과를 연결함
examples: If you heat ice, it melts.

grammar.en: Follow a present if clause with an imperative.
grammar.desc: 현재형 if절 뒤 명령문으로 조건부 지시를 구성함
examples: If you feel tired, take a break.

grammar.key: IF CLAUSE + IMPERATIVE, HEDGING (if, if-, if you want, like, prefer)
grammar.en: Soften an instruction with if you want or prefer.
grammar.desc: if you want 등으로 지시와 제안의 직접성을 줄임
examples: Take a seat if you like.

grammar.en: Build a conditional if clause in the present simple.
grammar.desc: if 뒤 현재형으로 조건 종속절을 구성함
examples: If I have time, I'll call you.

grammar.en: Use could in affirmative statements.
grammar.desc: could를 사용한 긍정절을 구성함
examples: I could swim when I was young.

grammar.en: Negate could with could not or couldn't.
grammar.desc: could not과 couldn't로 부정절을 구성함
examples: I couldn't open the door.

grammar.en: Form questions with could before the subject.
grammar.desc: could를 주어 앞에 놓아 의문문을 구성함
examples: Could you help me?

grammar.key: AS YOU KNOW, ORGANISING, MARKING SHARED KNOWLEDGE (as you know)
grammar.en: Mark shared knowledge with as you know.
grammar.desc: as you know로 공유하는 정보를 표시함
examples: As you know, the office closes at five.

grammar.en: State or ask about intentions with be going to.
grammar.desc: be going to로 의도를 서술하거나 질문함
examples: I'm going to visit my aunt.

grammar.key: WITH TO INFINITIVE, SPECIFYING (to, something, anything)
grammar.en: Specify something or anything with a to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: something과 anything을 to부정사로 구체화함
examples: I need something to drink.

grammar.en: Put an adjective after something or anything.
grammar.desc: something과 anything 뒤 형용사로 수식함
examples: Do you have anything cheaper?

grammar.en: Use something to refer to an unspecified thing.
grammar.desc: something으로 특정하지 않은 대상을 가리킴
examples: I heard something outside.

grammar.en: Use anything after a negative verb.
grammar.desc: 부정형 동사 뒤 anything을 사용함
examples: I didn't buy anything.

grammar.en: Use someone and everyone with a singular verb.
grammar.desc: someone과 everyone 주어에 단수 동사를 사용함
examples: Everyone knows the answer.

grammar.en: Add else after an indefinite pronoun.
grammar.desc: 부정대명사 뒤 else로 다른 대상을 나타냄
examples: Would you like something else?

grammar.key: DETERMINERS ANY, MUCH, MANY (any, much, many)
grammar.en: Use any, much and many in negative noun phrases.
grammar.desc: 부정문 명사구에 any·much·many를 사용함
examples: I don't have many pencils.

grammar.en: Give a negative instruction with don't and a verb.
grammar.desc: don't와 동사 원형으로 부정 명령문을 구성함
examples: Don't touch that button.

grammar.en: Use 's to mark a singular noun's possession.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사 뒤 's를 붙여 소유를 나타냄
examples: This is Daniel's bicycle.

grammar.en: Use was and a participle for past passive statements.
grammar.desc: 단수 주어 뒤 was와 과거분사로 수동문을 구성함
examples: The window was repaired yesterday.

grammar.en: Identify a passive agent with by.
grammar.desc: 수동문에서 by로 행위자를 나타냄
examples: The window was repaired by Alex.

grammar.en: Use is and a participle for present passive statements.
grammar.desc: 단수 주어 뒤 is와 과거분사로 수동문을 구성함
examples: This cheese is made locally.

grammar.en: Form affirmative past-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: was·were와 ing형으로 긍정 과거진행절을 구성함
examples: I was reading at eight.

grammar.en: Use past continuous to set a past-event background.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형으로 주된 과거 사건의 배경을 나타냄
examples: I was reading when the phone rang.

grammar.en: Put mid-position adverbs in past-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: 과거진행절의 중간 위치에 부사를 사용함
examples: She was quietly reading a book.

grammar.en: Build negative past-simple statements.
grammar.desc: 기본 동사를 사용한 단순과거 부정문을 구성함
examples: I didn't visit the museum.

grammar.en: Use past simple in a when subordinate clause.
grammar.desc: when 종속절에 단순과거를 사용함
examples: When I arrived, the shop was closed.

grammar.en: Ask past-simple questions with you as subject.
grammar.desc: you를 주어로 단순과거 의문문을 구성함
examples: Did you enjoy the concert?

grammar.en: Follow enjoy with an -ing form.
grammar.desc: enjoy 뒤에 동명사를 사용함
examples: I enjoy swimming.

grammar.en: Use yours as object or complement with singular reference.
grammar.desc: yours를 단수 소유 대상의 목적어·보어로 사용함
examples: I have my pen. Can I borrow yours too?

grammar.en: Use mine in subject, object and complement positions.
grammar.desc: mine을 소유 대상의 주어·목적어·보어로 사용함
examples: That blue coat is mine.

grammar.key: + OF MINE (of mine, mine, of, a friend of mine, friends of mine)
grammar.en: Use a friend of mine and friends of mine.
grammar.desc: of mine으로 본인의 친구에 해당함을 나타냄
examples: A friend of mine lives nearby.

grammar.en: Put just before a preposition to refine location.
grammar.desc: 전치사 앞 just로 위치 관계를 더 정확히 나타냄
examples: The cafe is just across the street.

grammar.en: Describe temporary situations in the present continuous.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형으로 일시적인 상황을 나타냄
examples: I'm staying with my cousin this week.

grammar.en: Use continuous always to emphasize recurrent behavior.
grammar.desc: 진행형과 always로 반복되는 행동을 강조함
examples: He is always losing his keys.

grammar.en: Ask present-continuous wh-questions in correspondence.
grammar.desc: 서신 등에서 현재진행형 의문사 질문을 구성함
examples: What are you doing this weekend?

grammar.en: Express a future hope with I hope.
grammar.desc: I hope 현재형으로 미래의 희망을 나타냄
examples: I hope you enjoy your holiday.

grammar.en: Use I or we with have and a past participle.
grammar.desc: I·we 뒤 have와 과거분사로 현재완료를 구성함
examples: I've finished my homework.

grammar.en: Use negative present perfect with for for a continuing absence.
grammar.desc: 현재완료 부정형과 for로 지속되는 미발생을 나타냄
examples: I haven't seen her for two weeks.

grammar.en: Use yet in a negative present-perfect statement.
grammar.desc: 현재완료 부정문에 yet으로 아직 미완료임을 나타냄
examples: I haven't finished yet.

grammar.en: Ask Have you questions with a past participle.
grammar.desc: Have you 뒤 과거분사로 현재완료 질문을 구성함
examples: Have you finished your homework?

grammar.en: Use I haven't with a past participle.
grammar.desc: I haven't 뒤 과거분사로 현재완료를 부정함
examples: I haven't read the book.

grammar.en: Give procedural directions in the present simple.
grammar.desc: 현재형으로 절차와 방향을 안내함
examples: You turn left at the bank and then cross the bridge.

grammar.key: REAL AND IMAGINED SITUATIONS AFTER IF (if)
grammar.en: Use present simple after if for possible situations.
grammar.desc: if 뒤 현재형으로 실제·가상 상황을 나타냄
examples: If she arrives early, we can have lunch.

grammar.en: Use frequency adverbs with the present simple.
grammar.desc: 현재형에 불특정 빈도 부사를 사용함
examples: I usually walk to work.

grammar.en: Use think, hope and know in the present simple.
grammar.desc: think·hope·know 등 정신활동 동사를 현재형으로 사용함
examples: I think this plan will work.

grammar.key: INDIRECT QUESTIONS (do you know, how, where, why)
grammar.en: Embed a wh-question after Do you know.
grammar.desc: Do you know 뒤 의문사 간접의문문을 구성함
examples: Do you know where the station is?

grammar.key: WITH OF + OBJECT PRONOUN (of, all, both)
grammar.en: Refer to quantity with all or both of an object pronoun.
grammar.desc: all·both of 뒤 목적격 대명사로 수량을 나타냄
examples: Both of them are ready.

grammar.en: Use object any to refer back in negative clauses.
grammar.desc: 부정절에서 any를 대상을 받는 목적어로 사용함
examples: I bought apples, but I didn't eat any.

grammar.en: Use pronoun some as subject or object.
grammar.desc: some을 수량을 받는 주어·목적어로 사용함
examples: We have rice. Some is in the cupboard.

grammar.en: Refer to quantity with pronouns some and any.
grammar.desc: 대명사 some·any로 수량을 나타냄
examples: I have some, but she doesn't have any.

grammar.key: SAME SUBJECT AND OBJECT. (myself, yourself, enjoy, buy)
grammar.en: Use a reflexive when subject and object coincide.
grammar.desc: 주어와 목적어가 같을 때 재귀대명사를 사용함
examples: I bought myself a new coat.

grammar.key: REPORTED STATEMENTS WITH TELL, PRONOUN SHIFT (tell, that-)
grammar.en: Report a statement with tell, an object and that.
grammar.desc: tell 뒤 목적어와 that절로 말을 전달함
examples: She told me that she was tired.

grammar.key: REPORTED STATEMENTS WITH SAY, PRONOUN SHIFT (say, that-)
grammar.en: Report a statement with say and a that-clause.
grammar.desc: say 뒤 that절로 말을 전달하며 대명사를 조정함
examples: He said that he was ready.

grammar.en: Give advice with should.
grammar.desc: should로 권고와 조언을 제시함
examples: You should take a break.

grammar.en: Build questions with should.
grammar.desc: should를 사용한 의문문을 구성함
examples: Should we call a taxi?

grammar.en: Use should not or shouldn't before a verb.
grammar.desc: should not과 shouldn't로 부정절을 구성함
examples: You shouldn't drive so fast.

grammar.en: Omit I before hope in informal messages.
grammar.desc: 비격식 메시지에서 hope 앞 주어 I를 생략함
examples: Hope you feel better soon.

grammar.en: Use a determiner and modifier before one.
grammar.desc: 대명사 one 앞에 한정사와 수식어를 사용함
examples: I prefer the blue one.

grammar.en: Substitute one for a known singular count noun.
grammar.desc: 이미 알려진 단수 가산명사를 one으로 대신함
examples: I lost my pen. Can I borrow one?

grammar.en: Specify the one with a following complement.
grammar.desc: the one 뒤 보충어로 특정 대상을 나타냄
examples: I want the small one on the top shelf.

grammar.en: Add a short question tag to a statement.
grammar.desc: 서술문 뒤 짧은 부가의문문을 덧붙임
examples: You're ready, aren't you?

grammar.key: THERE IS/ARE + A LOT OF (there is, are, there are, a lot of)
grammar.en: Use there is or there are with a lot of.
grammar.desc: there is·are 뒤 a lot of로 다수의 존재를 나타냄
examples: There are a lot of books here.

grammar.en: Use there is before an uncountable noun.
grammar.desc: there is 뒤 불가산 명사로 존재를 나타냄
examples: There is water on the floor.

grammar.key: WITH DETERMINERS, QUANTITY (some, any, a lot of, more)
grammar.en: Quantify uncountable nouns with quantity expressions.
grammar.desc: 수량 표현으로 불가산 명사를 한정함
examples: We need a little more water.

grammar.en: Ask a wh-question with main verb be.
grammar.desc: 의문사와 본동사 be로 의문문을 구성함
examples: Where is the entrance?

grammar.en: Ask a wh-question with auxiliary do.
grammar.desc: 의문사와 조동사 do로 일반동사 질문을 구성함
examples: Why do you walk to work?

grammar.en: Suggest an action with Why don't you or we.
grammar.desc: Why don't you·we로 행동을 제안함
examples: Why don't we eat outside?

grammar.en: Ask wh-questions with auxiliary have.
grammar.desc: 의문사와 조동사 have로 완료형 질문을 구성함
examples: What have you bought?

grammar.en: Offer help or express willingness with will.
grammar.desc: will로 도움 제안과 자발적 의사를 나타냄
examples: I'll carry your bag for you.

grammar.en: Use will in question clauses.
grammar.desc: will을 사용한 의문절을 구성함
examples: Will you arrive before lunch?

grammar.key: AFTER IF, FUTURE SITUATIONS (will, won't, if, if-)
grammar.en: Use will after an if-clause for a possible future.
grammar.desc: if절 뒤 주절에 will로 가능한 미래 결과를 나타냄
examples: If it rains, we will stay inside.

grammar.en: Negate will with won't or will not.
grammar.desc: will not과 won't로 부정문을 구성함
examples: I won't attend the meeting.

grammar.en: Use would not or wouldn't before a verb.
grammar.desc: would not과 wouldn't로 부정문을 구성함
examples: I wouldn't choose that hotel.

grammar.key: SUGGESTIONS WITH IT WOULD BE (would, wouldn't, it would be)
grammar.en: Make a suggestion with It would be.
grammar.desc: It would be로 바람직한 행동을 제안함
examples: It would be better to book early.

grammar.key: QUESTIONS WITH LIKE (would, wouldn't, like, would you like)
grammar.en: Ask about wishes with Would you like.
grammar.desc: Would you like로 상대방의 희망을 질문함
examples: Would you like some tea?

grammar.en: Form affirmative clauses with would.
grammar.desc: would를 사용한 긍정절을 구성함
examples: I would enjoy living near the sea.

grammar.en: Describe an imagined situation with would.
grammar.desc: would로 가정한 상황을 나타냄
examples: If I had a garden, I would grow vegetables.

grammar.en: Express wishes or preferences with would and varied verbs.
grammar.desc: would와 여러 동사로 희망과 선호를 나타냄
examples: I would prefer to leave early.

grammar.en: Soften a request with if possible.
grammar.desc: if possible로 요청의 직접성을 줄임
examples: Please send the file today, if possible.

grammar.key: IT + BE + IMPORTANT + CLAUSE (it, be, important, that)
grammar.en: Assess importance with It is important that.
grammar.desc: It is important 뒤 that절로 중요성을 판단함
examples: It is important that everyone arrives on time.

grammar.key: DEGREE WITH VERBS (a little, a bit)
grammar.en: Modify verbs with a little or a bit.
grammar.desc: a little과 a bit으로 행동의 정도를 나타냄
examples: The delay worried me a little.

grammar.en: Indicate location with place adverbs.
grammar.desc: near·upstairs 등 장소 부사로 위치를 나타냄
examples: The children are playing upstairs.

grammar.key: STANCE (completely, obviously, clearly, actually, luckily, honestly, sadly, basically, hopefully)
grammar.en: Use stance adverbs to present a viewpoint.
grammar.desc: clearly·luckily 등 태도 부사로 관점을 제시함
examples: Luckily, nobody was injured.

grammar.en: Link ideas with therefore, furthermore or otherwise.
grammar.desc: therefore·furthermore·otherwise로 문장을 연결함
examples: The road is closed; therefore, we must take another route.

grammar.en: End an alternative question with or not.
grammar.desc: 선택 의문문 끝에 or not을 사용함
examples: Are you coming or not?

grammar.en: Use another to refer to a different item.
grammar.desc: another로 다른 대상을 가리킴
examples: This coat is too big. Could I try another one?

grammar.en: Put another before a singular noun.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사 앞에 another를 사용함
examples: We need another chair.

grammar.en: Use another to request or describe one more.
grammar.desc: another로 하나 더 추가되는 대상을 나타냄
examples: Could I have another cup of tea?

grammar.en: Use the other for the remaining or opposite item.
grammar.desc: the other로 나머지나 반대쪽 대상을 나타냄
examples: One shoe is here; the other shoe is under the bed.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (can, cannot, can't, also, always, even, just, only, really, still)
grammar.en: Place a mid-position adverb after can.
grammar.desc: can 뒤 중간 위치에 부사를 사용함
examples: You can also borrow a bicycle.

grammar.key: GENERAL TRUTHS AND TENDENCIES (can, cannot, can't, can be)
grammar.en: Describe general tendencies with can be.
grammar.desc: can be로 일반적인 경향과 사실을 나타냄
examples: Winters here can be very cold.

grammar.key: SURPRISE (can, cannot, can't, can you believe)
grammar.en: Express surprise with Can you believe.
grammar.desc: Can you believe로 놀라움을 나타냄
examples: Can you believe how quickly she finished?

grammar.en: Use can't in negative questions and tags.
grammar.desc: can't로 부정 질문과 부가의문문을 구성함
examples: Can't we leave earlier?

grammar.en: Use compound adjectives such as well-known.
grammar.desc: well-known 등 합성 형용사를 사용함
examples: That well-known singer lives nearby.

grammar.en: Join different comparative adjectives with and.
grammar.desc: and로 서로 다른 비교급 형용사를 연결함
examples: The new room is bigger and brighter.

grammar.key: COMBINING THE SAME COMPARATIVE ADJECTIVE WITH AND (and, become)
grammar.en: Repeat a comparative with and to show change.
grammar.desc: 비교급을 and로 반복하여 점진적인 변화를 나타냄
examples: The weather is getting colder and colder.

grammar.en: Intensify a predicative comparative with much.
grammar.desc: 보어 비교급 앞 much로 차이의 정도를 강조함
examples: This seat is much more comfortable.

grammar.en: Follow the best with a present-perfect clause.
grammar.desc: the best 뒤 현재완료절로 유일한 경험을 비교함
examples: This is the best that I have ever tasted.

grammar.en: Soften a comparative with a little bit.
grammar.desc: a little bit으로 비교의 차이가 작음을 나타냄
examples: This bag is a little bit lighter.

grammar.en: Express a result with so, an adjective and that.
grammar.desc: so와 형용사 뒤 that절로 정도와 결과를 연결함
examples: The room was so cold that we wore our coats.

grammar.en: Compare with an -ing clause after than.
grammar.desc: than 뒤 ing 비정형절로 비교 대상을 제시함
examples: Walking is healthier than sitting all day.

grammar.en: Compare with a finite clause after than.
grammar.desc: than 뒤 정형절로 비교 대상을 제시함
examples: The room was smaller than I expected.

grammar.en: Compare equality with adjective or adverb between as.
grammar.desc: as와 as 사이 형용사·부사로 동등성을 비교함
examples: She is as tall as I am.

grammar.en: Use too and an adjective before a to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: too와 형용사 뒤 to부정사로 과도한 정도를 나타냄
examples: This box is too heavy to lift.

grammar.en: Use repeated comparatives after get or become.
grammar.desc: get·become 뒤 반복 비교급으로 변화를 나타냄
examples: The evenings are getting longer and longer.

grammar.en: Intensify a comparative with even.
grammar.desc: even으로 비교급의 차이를 강조함
examples: The next train is even faster.

grammar.key: LINKING VERB + LIKE OR SIMILAR TO (like, similar to)
grammar.en: Use like or similar to after a linking verb.
grammar.desc: 연결동사 뒤 like·similar to로 유사성을 나타냄
examples: The new model looks similar to the old one.

grammar.key: IF + PAST PERFECT + WOULD HAVE + -ED, IMAGINED SITUATION, REGRET|(THIRD CONDITIONAL) (if, would have)
grammar.en: Imagine a different past with if had and would have.
grammar.desc: 과거완료 if절과 would have로 과거를 가정함
examples: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.

grammar.en: Connect several main clauses in a narrative.
grammar.desc: 이야기에서 여러 주절을 접속사로 연결함
examples: I opened the door, and she came in, but nobody spoke.

grammar.key: COMBINING CLAUSES OF THE SAME TYPE
grammar.en: Coordinate clauses of the same grammatical type.
grammar.desc: 같은 문법 유형의 절을 접속사로 연결함
examples: I waited until she arrived and until the rain stopped.

grammar.en: Use plus to coordinate nouns or numbers.
grammar.desc: plus로 명사나 수를 병렬 연결함
examples: The room costs fifty pounds plus tax.

grammar.key: BE ABLE TO, PAST (be able to, was able to, were able to)
grammar.en: Describe past capability with was or were able to.
grammar.desc: was·were able to로 과거 능력을 나타냄
examples: I was able to finish the task yesterday.

grammar.key: MODAL WITH BE ABLE TO (be able to)
grammar.en: Use a modal before be able to and a verb.
grammar.desc: 조동사 뒤 be able to와 동사로 능력을 나타냄
examples: We may be able to help tomorrow.

grammar.key: BE ALLOWED TO, PERMISSION (be allowed to)
grammar.en: Express permission with be allowed to.
grammar.desc: be allowed to로 허용을 나타냄
examples: Students are allowed to use this room.

grammar.key: BE SUPPOSED TO, PAST EXPECTATION (be supposed to, was supposed to, were supposed to)
grammar.en: Describe past expectations with was supposed to.
grammar.desc: was·were supposed to로 과거의 예정·기대를 나타냄
examples: I was supposed to meet her yesterday, but she cancelled.

grammar.key: BE EXPRESSIONS (be, be allowed to, be supposed to, be able to, will)
grammar.en: Vary be in able, allowed and supposed to expressions.
grammar.desc: be able·allowed·supposed to의 be형을 변화시킴
examples: We will be allowed to enter after nine.

grammar.en: Use won't in a future-continuous clause.
grammar.desc: won't be와 ing형으로 미래진행형을 부정함
examples: I won't be working tomorrow evening.

grammar.en: Form future-continuous affirmatives with will or shall.
grammar.desc: will·shall be와 ing형으로 미래진행형을 구성함
examples: We shall be travelling all day tomorrow.

grammar.en: Use would for a future viewed from the past.
grammar.desc: would로 과거 시점에서 본 미래를 나타냄
examples: She said that she would arrive at six.

grammar.key: BE GOING TO (be going to, be, going to)
grammar.en: Use was going to for a future viewed from the past.
grammar.desc: was·were going to로 과거 시점의 미래를 나타냄
examples: I was going to call you later.

grammar.en: Describe fixed plans with will and scheduled times.
grammar.desc: will과 정해진 시각으로 확정된 계획을 나타냄
examples: The coach will leave at seven on Friday.

grammar.en: Make a prediction with will or 'll.
grammar.desc: will과 'll로 앞으로의 일을 예측함
examples: The weather will improve tomorrow.

grammar.key: IMMEDIATE PLANS WITH SHALL (shall, i, we)
grammar.en: Use shall with I or we for immediate plans.
grammar.desc: I·we와 shall로 즉각적인 계획을 나타냄
examples: I shall take a taxi now.

grammar.en: Negate future intentions with be not going to.
grammar.desc: be not going to로 미래 의도를 부정함
examples: I'm not going to buy that car.

grammar.en: Put an adverb after be before going to.
grammar.desc: be와 going to 사이에 부사를 사용함
examples: We are definitely going to move.

grammar.en: Use past be with going to.
grammar.desc: going to 앞 be를 과거형으로 사용함
examples: They were going to meet us at noon.

grammar.key: INFINITIVE (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Use have to in an infinitive position.
grammar.desc: 부정사 위치에 have to를 사용함
examples: I don't want to have to wait outside.

grammar.key: I HAVE TO ADMIT (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to, i have to admit)
grammar.en: Emphasize an admission with I have to admit.
grammar.desc: I have to admit으로 인정하는 내용을 강조함
examples: I have to admit that I was wrong.

grammar.en: Add do before an imperative verb for emphasis.
grammar.desc: 명령 동사 앞 do를 덧붙여 강조함
examples: Do take a seat.

grammar.en: Use an imperative as an invitation or offer.
grammar.desc: 명령문 형식으로 초대와 제공을 나타냄
examples: Come in and have some tea.

grammar.en: Introduce a point with Let me and a verb.
grammar.desc: Let me 뒤 동사 원형으로 발화 내용을 도입함
examples: Let me explain the problem.

grammar.en: Use a wh-word as subject without auxiliary do.
grammar.desc: 의문사를 주어로 쓰고 do 없이 질문을 구성함
examples: Who called you?

grammar.en: Put an adverb between a question's subject and verb.
grammar.desc: 의문문의 주어와 본동사 사이에 부사를 사용함
examples: Do you usually work late?

grammar.en: Ask about selection or possession with which or whose.
grammar.desc: which·whose로 선택과 소유를 질문함
examples: Whose coat is this?

grammar.en: Use may not in negative statements.
grammar.desc: may not으로 부정문을 구성함
examples: She may not attend today.

grammar.en: Place an adverb immediately after may.
grammar.desc: may 뒤 중간 위치에 부사를 사용함
examples: You may also bring a friend.

grammar.en: Ask a question with May I.
grammar.desc: May I로 질문을 구성함
examples: May I sit here?

grammar.en: Shift may to might in reported speech.
grammar.desc: 간접화법에서 may를 might로 전환함
examples: She said that she might be late.

grammar.key: POSSIBILITY IN THE PAST (might, might have)
grammar.en: Speculate about the past with might have and a participle.
grammar.desc: might have와 과거분사로 과거의 가능성을 추측함
examples: He might have missed the bus.

grammar.en: Form affirmative might have clauses.
grammar.desc: might have 뒤 과거분사로 긍정절을 구성함
examples: She might have left already.

grammar.en: Use might not before a verb.
grammar.desc: might not으로 부정절을 구성함
examples: I might not come tomorrow.

grammar.en: Place enough after an adjective.
grammar.desc: 형용사 뒤 enough로 충분한 정도를 나타냄
examples: The room is warm enough.

grammar.en: Use quite a before an adjective and noun.
grammar.desc: quite a 뒤 형용사와 명사로 정도를 나타냄
examples: It was quite a difficult task.

grammar.key: DEDUCTIONS AND CONCLUSIONS (must, mustn't, it must be, you must be)
grammar.en: Draw a strong deduction with must be.
grammar.desc: must be로 근거에 따른 강한 추측을 나타냄
examples: The lights are off; they must be asleep.

grammar.en: Place an adverb after must.
grammar.desc: must 뒤 중간 위치에 부사를 사용함
examples: You must also sign this form.

grammar.key: FRIEND + OF + POSSESSIVE DETERMINER + NOUN (of, a friend of, friends of)
grammar.en: Use a friend of followed by a possessive noun phrase.
grammar.desc: a friend of 뒤 소유 한정 명사구로 관계를 나타냄
examples: A friend of my brother is visiting.

grammar.key: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE ‘S + NOUN ('s, of)
grammar.en: Build an of-phrase containing a possessive noun phrase.
grammar.desc: of구 안에 's 소유 명사구를 넣어 명사구를 구성함
examples: The roof of my neighbour's house needs repairs.

grammar.en: Focus an idea with fronted The thing and a clause.
grammar.desc: 문두 The thing 뒤 절로 발화의 초점을 제시함
examples: The thing I worry about is the cost.

grammar.en: Give advice with You ought to.
grammar.desc: You ought to로 상대방에게 조언함
examples: You ought to rest today.

grammar.en: Form affirmative ought to clauses.
grammar.desc: ought to를 사용한 긍정절을 구성함
examples: We ought to book in advance.

grammar.en: Describe repeated past behavior with continuous always.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형과 always로 과거의 반복 행동을 나타냄
examples: She was always losing her keys.

grammar.en: Give a reason in a past-continuous because clause.
grammar.desc: because절의 과거진행형으로 이유를 나타냄
examples: I closed the window because cold air was coming in.

grammar.en: Give earlier background with past perfect continuous.
grammar.desc: 과거완료진행형으로 앞서 시작된 배경 동작을 나타냄
examples: She had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.

grammar.en: Form affirmative past-perfect-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: had been과 ing형으로 긍정 과거완료진행형을 만듦
examples: She had been waiting for an hour.

grammar.en: Exclaim with How followed by an adjective.
grammar.desc: How 뒤 형용사로 감탄을 나타냄
examples: How wonderful!

grammar.en: Follow How and an adjective with a clause.
grammar.desc: How와 형용사 뒤 절로 감탄문을 구성함
examples: How quiet the garden is!

grammar.en: Put an adjective after an indefinite pronoun.
grammar.desc: 부정대명사 뒤 형용사구로 수식함
examples: We need somewhere quiet.

grammar.en: Use an adjective as object complement after make.
grammar.desc: make 뒤 목적격 형용사 보어로 상태 변화를 나타냄
examples: The news made her happy.

grammar.key: ADJECTIVES WITH PREFIX A- (a-, asleep, awake, alive, alone)
grammar.en: Use asleep, awake, alive or alone predicatively.
grammar.desc: asleep·awake·alive·alone을 서술 보어로 사용함
examples: The baby is asleep.

grammar.key: COMPARATIVE CLAUSES WITH MINE, YOURS (mine, yours)
grammar.en: Use mine or yours after as in an equality comparison.
grammar.desc: as 동등 비교절에 mine·yours를 사용함
examples: My bag is as heavy as yours.

grammar.en: Add 's to an irregular plural noun for possession.
grammar.desc: 불규칙 복수 명사 뒤 's로 소유를 나타냄
examples: The children's coats are wet.

grammar.en: Use their as a possessive determiner.
grammar.desc: their를 소유 한정사로 사용함
examples: Their house is near the station.

grammar.en: Describe arrangements with varied continuous verbs.
grammar.desc: 다양한 동사의 현재진행형으로 미래 일정을 나타냄
examples: We are flying to Madrid next week.

grammar.en: Ask about future plans with varied continuous verbs.
grammar.desc: 다양한 동사의 현재진행형으로 미래 계획을 질문함
examples: Are you joining us for dinner tomorrow?

grammar.en: Use present perfect and just for a recent event.
grammar.desc: 현재완료와 just로 최근에 완료한 일을 나타냄
examples: I have just finished lunch.

grammar.key: WITH UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS (a little, a bit of, a little bit of)
grammar.en: Quantify mass nouns with a little or a bit of.
grammar.desc: a little·a bit of로 불가산 명사의 수량을 나타냄
examples: Add a little salt.

grammar.key: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS (most, enough, plenty of, loads of)
grammar.en: Use most, enough, plenty of or loads of with nouns.
grammar.desc: most·enough 등으로 복수·불가산 명사를 한정함
examples: We have enough chairs and plenty of water.

grammar.en: Use much before mass nouns in questions.
grammar.desc: 질문에서 불가산 명사 앞에 much를 사용함
examples: Do you have much luggage?

grammar.en: Use many before plural nouns in questions.
grammar.desc: 질문에서 복수 명사 앞에 many를 사용함
examples: Do you have many visitors?

grammar.key: SO MUCH, TOO MUCH WITH UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS (so much, too much)
grammar.en: Use so much or too much before mass nouns.
grammar.desc: 불가산 명사 앞 so much·too much로 수량을 나타냄
examples: There is too much sugar in this tea.

grammar.key: DETERMINER + OF + DETERMINER (of, half of, enough of, none of)
grammar.en: Use half, enough or none with of and a determiner.
grammar.desc: half·enough·none 뒤 of와 한정사를 사용함
examples: Half of the students are absent.

grammar.key: WITH PLURAL NOUNS (several, millions of, a few of)
grammar.en: Use varied quantifiers before plural nouns.
grammar.desc: several 등 다양한 수량 한정사로 복수 명사를 한정함
examples: Several shops are closed.

grammar.en: Use object who in a non-defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 비제한적 관계절에서 who를 목적어로 사용함
examples: My aunt, who you met yesterday, is visiting.

grammar.en: Use object who or that in a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: 제한적 관계절에서 who·that을 목적어로 사용함
examples: The person who I met was very helpful.

grammar.en: Define a time noun with a when relative clause.
grammar.desc: 시간 명사를 when 관계절로 수식함
examples: Friday is the day when we meet.

grammar.key: THE + NOUN + WHO/THAT, FOCUS (the, who, that)
grammar.en: Focus a person or thing with a defining relative clause.
grammar.desc: the person who 등 관계절 명사구로 초점을 나타냄
examples: The person who handles bookings is Mia.

grammar.en: Define a place noun with a where relative clause.
grammar.desc: 장소 명사를 where 관계절로 수식함
examples: This is the cafe where we met.

grammar.key: THE REASON WHY, FOCUS (the reason why, why, reason)
grammar.en: Explain a reason with the reason why.
grammar.desc: the reason why로 이유를 설명함
examples: The reason why I left was the noise.

grammar.key: REPORTED YES-NO QUESTIONS (yes-no, ask, if, whether)
grammar.en: Report a yes-no question with ask and if or whether.
grammar.desc: ask 뒤 if·whether절로 예·아니요 질문을 전달함
examples: She asked whether I was ready.

grammar.en: Seek advice with shall in a question.
grammar.desc: shall 의문문으로 조언을 구함
examples: What shall we do next?

grammar.en: Express past regret with should have and a participle.
grammar.desc: should have와 과거분사로 과거의 후회를 나타냄
examples: I should have called you earlier.

grammar.key: NARRATIVE DEVICE (should, shouldn't, you should have)
grammar.en: Emphasize a story point with You should have.
grammar.desc: You should have와 과거분사로 이야기 내용을 강조함
examples: You should have seen her face when we arrived!

grammar.en: Use should to predict a likely event.
grammar.desc: should로 일어날 가능성이 높은 일을 나타냄
examples: The parcel should arrive tomorrow.

grammar.en: Build affirmative should have clauses.
grammar.desc: should have 뒤 과거분사로 긍정절을 구성함
examples: We should have booked earlier.

grammar.en: Accept a gift politely with You shouldn't have.
grammar.desc: You shouldn't have로 선물에 대한 감사의 뜻을 나타냄
examples: Thank you for the gift. You shouldn't have bought me anything!

grammar.en: Describe an ideal situation with should.
grammar.desc: should로 이상적이거나 바람직한 상황을 나타냄
examples: Everyone should have a safe place to live.

grammar.en: Build negative should have clauses.
grammar.desc: shouldn't have 뒤 과거분사로 과거를 부정함
examples: I shouldn't have spoken so loudly.

grammar.en: Use shouldn't in a tag to seek agreement or advice.
grammar.desc: shouldn't 부가의문문으로 의견이나 동의를 구함
examples: We should leave now, shouldn't we?

grammar.en: Use before or after with an -ing subordinate clause.
grammar.desc: before·after 뒤 ing 종속절로 시간을 나타냄
examples: Wash your hands before eating.

grammar.en: Follow a main clause with a reason clause.
grammar.desc: 주절 뒤 이유 접속사가 이끄는 종속절을 사용함
examples: We stayed inside because the road was flooded.

grammar.en: Use although or while clauses to show contrast.
grammar.desc: although·while 등의 종속절로 대조를 나타냄
examples: Although it was raining, we went outside.

grammar.en: Use one of the with a superlative and plural noun.
grammar.desc: one of the 뒤 최상급과 복수 명사를 사용함
examples: This is one of the oldest buildings in town.

grammar.key: THE BEST WITH NOUN AND TO- INFINITIVE (the best, to-, to)
grammar.en: Use the best with a noun and to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: the best 뒤 명사와 to부정사로 최상급을 나타냄
examples: This is the best place to watch the sunset.

grammar.key: THE BEST WITH NOUN AND PRESENT PERFECT (the best)
grammar.en: Use the best noun with a present-perfect clause.
grammar.desc: the best 명사 뒤 현재완료절로 경험을 비교함
examples: This is the best meal I have ever eaten.

grammar.en: Make a request more polite with Could you possibly.
grammar.desc: Could you possibly로 요청의 격식을 높임
examples: Could you possibly open the window?

grammar.en: Join two alternative question clauses with or.
grammar.desc: or로 의문절 둘을 연결하여 선택을 질문함
examples: Will you walk, or will you take a bus?

grammar.en: Join two alternative question phrases with or.
grammar.desc: or로 구 둘을 연결하여 선택을 질문함
examples: Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat?

grammar.key: THE SAME (+ NOUN) + AS + PRONOUN OR NOUN (the same, as)
grammar.en: Express identity with the same noun as.
grammar.desc: the same 명사 뒤 as로 동일성을 나타냄
examples: My bag is the same colour as yours.

grammar.en: Use rather than before a noun or prepositional phrase.
grammar.desc: rather than 뒤 명사구·전치사구로 선택을 대조함
examples: I chose tea rather than coffee.

grammar.key: ELLIPTED IF NOT, ALTERNATIVE (if not, yes-no)
grammar.en: Offer an alternative with the abbreviated clause If not.
grammar.desc: 축약 조건절 If not으로 대안을 제시함
examples: Can you come today? If not, we can meet tomorrow.

grammar.key: IF + PAST SIMPLE + WOULD, FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION|(SECOND CONDITIONAL) (if, would)
grammar.en: Imagine a situation with past if and would clauses.
grammar.desc: 과거형 if절과 would 주절로 가상 상황을 나타냄
examples: If I had more time, I would learn to cook.

grammar.key: ELLIPTED IF SO, CONFIRMING (if so, yes-no)
grammar.en: Refer to an affirmative possibility with If so.
grammar.desc: 축약 조건절 If so로 앞선 긍정 가능성을 받음
examples: Have you booked? If so, please send the details.

grammar.key: PRESENT SIMPLE IF CLAUSE + MODAL, FUTURE, POSSIBLE OUTCOME (if)
grammar.en: Link a future present-if condition to a modal result.
grammar.desc: 현재형 if절과 조동사 주절로 가능 결과를 나타냄
examples: If it rains, we might stay home.

grammar.key: IF + PAST SIMPLE + COULD, FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION (if, could)
grammar.en: Imagine a possible action with past if and could.
grammar.desc: 과거형 if절과 could로 가상 행동 가능성을 나타냄
examples: If we had a car, we could visit the coast.

grammar.key: IF I WERE YOU + WOULD, FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION (if i were you, would)
grammar.en: Give hypothetical advice with If I were you, I would.
grammar.desc: If I were you와 would로 가정에 기반하여 조언함
examples: If I were you, I would call her.

grammar.key: PRESENT CONTINUOUS IF CLAUSE , PLANS & ADVICE (if, going to)
grammar.en: Use if plus a continuous plan before advice.
grammar.desc: if절의 진행형·going to 계획 뒤 조언을 제시함
examples: If you are going to drive tonight, you should rest first.

grammar.key: PRESENT SIMPLE IF CLAUSE + WILL, FUTURE, LIKELY OUTCOME (FIRST CONDITIONAL) (if, will)
grammar.en: Use present if and will for a likely future result.
grammar.desc: 현재형 if절과 will로 가능한 미래 결과를 나타냄
examples: If you arrive early, we will have lunch together.

grammar.en: Express an exception with unless and present simple.
grammar.desc: unless 뒤 현재형으로 예외 조건을 나타냄
examples: We will leave at six unless it rains.

grammar.en: Add a further advantage in a clause with plus.
grammar.desc: plus로 절을 연결하여 추가 이점을 제시함
examples: The room is cheap; plus, it is near the station.

grammar.en: Use pronoun those with plural reference.
grammar.desc: those를 복수 대상을 가리키는 대명사로 사용함
examples: Those are my keys over there.

grammar.en: Use pronoun those for previously mentioned things.
grammar.desc: 대명사 those로 이미 언급한 대상을 받음
examples: I tried two coats, but those were too small.

grammar.en: Use pronoun these for relevant mentioned things.
grammar.desc: 대명사 these로 현재 관련된 언급 대상을 받음
examples: We have two problems. These need our attention.

grammar.en: Use pronoun these with plural reference.
grammar.desc: these를 복수 대상을 가리키는 대명사로 사용함
examples: These are my keys.

grammar.key: THIS ONE, THAT ONE SUBSTITUTION (this one, that one)
grammar.en: Replace a known singular noun with this one or that one.
grammar.desc: this one·that one으로 앞선 단수 명사를 대신함
examples: I need a pen. Is this one yours?

grammar.key: ORGANISING, MARKING NEW KNOWLEDGE, INFORMAL (you see, the thing is)
grammar.en: Introduce new information with you see or the thing is.
grammar.desc: you see·the thing is로 새로운 정보를 도입함
examples: The thing is, I have already booked another room.

grammar.en: State negative plans with be not going to.
grammar.desc: be not going to로 실행하지 않을 계획을 나타냄
examples: I'm not going to move this year.

grammar.en: Use one for people generally in formal language.
grammar.desc: 격식 문장에서 one으로 일반적인 사람을 가리킴
examples: One should always check the details.

grammar.en: Build a passive with get and a past participle.
grammar.desc: get과 과거분사로 수동태를 구성함
examples: My bicycle got stolen yesterday.

grammar.en: Use something or nobody as a singular subject.
grammar.desc: something·nobody 주어에 단수 동사를 사용함
examples: Nobody knows the answer.

grammar.en: Use ever, never, yet and still in negative contexts.
grammar.desc: 부정 맥락에 ever·never·yet·still을 사용함
examples: I haven't finished yet.

grammar.en: Emphasize noun phrases with such a or such.
grammar.desc: such a·such 뒤 형용사 명사구로 강조함
examples: It was such a lovely day.

grammar.en: Use past passive with singular or plural subjects.
grammar.desc: 단수·복수 명사를 주어로 과거 수동태를 사용함
examples: The windows were repaired yesterday.

grammar.en: Focus the agent with by in a passive clause.
grammar.desc: 수동절의 by로 행위자에 초점을 둠
examples: The painting was restored by a local artist.

grammar.en: Make an indirect object the subject of a past passive.
grammar.desc: 두 목적어 동사의 간접목적어를 과거 수동 주어로 삼음
examples: She was given a ticket.

grammar.en: Use am, is or are being with a past participle.
grammar.desc: be being과 과거분사로 현재진행 수동태를 구성함
examples: The bridge is being repaired.

grammar.key: WITH BY IN A RELATIVE CLAUSE| (by)
grammar.en: Use a passive relative clause containing by.
grammar.desc: by를 포함한 수동 관계절로 정보를 추가함
examples: The book, which was written by a local teacher, is popular.

grammar.en: Use present-continuous passive for a future arrangement.
grammar.desc: 현재진행 수동태로 미래의 예정된 일을 나타냄
examples: The new tables are being delivered tomorrow.

grammar.en: Negate present-simple passive clauses.
grammar.desc: 현재형 수동태 부정절을 구성함
examples: These tickets aren't sold online.

grammar.en: Use present-simple passive with varied subjects.
grammar.desc: 다양한 주어로 현재형 수동태를 사용함
examples: The rooms are cleaned every day.

grammar.key: INFINITIVE (going to, have to, need to, want to)
grammar.en: Use a passive infinitive after want, need or have to.
grammar.desc: want·need·have to 등 뒤 수동 부정사를 사용함
examples: I want to be invited to the meeting.

grammar.en: Use varied mid-position adverbs in past continuous.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형의 중간 위치에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: She was carefully checking the list.

grammar.en: Form negative past-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형 부정절을 구성함
examples: I wasn't working at eight.

grammar.en: Form past-continuous questions.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형 의문문을 구성함
examples: Were you waiting outside?

grammar.en: Use past perfect in an if-clause for an imagined past.
grammar.desc: 과거완료 if절로 실제와 다른 과거를 가정함
examples: If I had known, I would have called.

grammar.en: Build affirmative past-perfect clauses.
grammar.desc: had와 과거분사로 긍정 과거완료절을 구성함
examples: She had finished before we arrived.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (never, ever, just, always, already)
grammar.en: Place never, just or already inside a past-perfect clause.
grammar.desc: 과거완료절 중간에 never·just·already 등을 사용함
examples: I had already sent the file.

grammar.en: Use past perfect for events before a past reference point.
grammar.desc: 과거완료로 과거 기준시점 이전의 일을 나타냄
examples: The train had left before I reached the station.

grammar.en: Sequence narrative events with past simple.
grammar.desc: 단순과거로 이야기 속 사건의 순서를 제시함
examples: I opened the door, took off my coat and sat down.

grammar.en: Use past simple after if for an imagined situation.
grammar.desc: if 뒤 과거형으로 현재·미래의 가상 상황을 나타냄
examples: If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle.

grammar.en: Describe past habits or states with past simple.
grammar.desc: 단순과거로 과거의 습관적 행동과 상태를 나타냄
examples: We walked to school every day that year.

grammar.en: Use wish with past simple for a different present.
grammar.desc: wish 뒤 과거형으로 현실과 다른 바람을 나타냄
examples: I wish I lived nearer the sea.

grammar.en: Use help plus an object and an optional-to infinitive.
grammar.desc: help 뒤 목적어와 to 유무가 가능한 부정사를 사용함
examples: She helped me carry the boxes.

grammar.key: MAKE, LET + INFINITIVE WITHOUT TO (make, let, to)
grammar.en: Follow make or let and an object with a bare infinitive.
grammar.desc: make·let 뒤 목적어와 동사 원형을 사용함
examples: They made us wait outside.

grammar.key: WOULD PREFER + TO, POLITENESS (would prefer, to)
grammar.en: State a preference politely with would prefer to.
grammar.desc: would prefer to로 선호를 정중하게 나타냄
examples: I would prefer to meet tomorrow.

grammar.en: Use yours after a noun and of.
grammar.desc: 명사와 of 뒤 yours로 소유 관계를 나타냄
examples: A friend of yours called earlier.

grammar.en: Use yours as a subject with singular reference.
grammar.desc: yours를 단수 소유 대상의 주어로 사용함
examples: Yours looks warmer than mine.

grammar.en: Use varied continuous verbs for temporary situations.
grammar.desc: 다양한 현재진행형 동사로 일시적 상황을 나타냄
examples: We are renovating our kitchen this month.

grammar.en: Describe temporary repeated acts with present continuous.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형으로 일시적으로 반복하는 행동을 나타냄
examples: I'm cycling to work every day this week.

grammar.key: WITH AS SOON AS (as soon as)
grammar.en: Use present simple after as soon as for future time.
grammar.desc: 미래 시간의 as soon as절에 현재형을 사용함
examples: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

grammar.en: Use present perfect continuous for ongoing repeated acts.
grammar.desc: 현재완료진행형으로 지속되는 반복 행동을 나타냄
examples: I've been taking swimming lessons every week.

grammar.en: Use present perfect continuous for one ongoing activity.
grammar.desc: 현재완료진행형으로 과거부터 이어지는 활동을 나타냄
examples: I've been waiting here for an hour.

grammar.en: Form negative present-perfect questions.
grammar.desc: 현재완료 부정 의문문을 구성함
examples: Haven't you finished yet?

grammar.en: Combine a superlative with present perfect.
grammar.desc: 최상급과 현재완료로 특별한 경험을 비교함
examples: This is the quietest place I have ever visited.

grammar.en: Use present perfect for an unfinished or indefinite period.
grammar.desc: 현재완료로 끝나지 않은 기간의 상태를 나타냄
examples: I have lived here for many years.

grammar.en: Emphasize early completion with already and present perfect.
grammar.desc: 현재완료와 already로 이미 완료한 일을 강조함
examples: I've already packed my bag.

grammar.en: Use present perfect and since for duration.
grammar.desc: 현재완료와 since로 기준시점부터의 지속을 나타냄
examples: I have known her since 2018.

grammar.en: Use present-simple say or show to report information.
grammar.desc: say·show 현재형으로 정보를 전달함
examples: The report shows that prices are falling.

grammar.key: NEGATIVE TAG QUESTIONS (don, or, t you agree)
grammar.en: Seek agreement with don't you think or agree.
grammar.desc: don't you think·agree로 의견과 동의를 구함
examples: It's a useful idea, don't you think?

grammar.en: Use remember, understand or believe in present simple.
grammar.desc: remember·understand·believe 등을 현재형으로 사용함
examples: I understand why you are worried.

grammar.en: Perform speech acts with present-simple verbs.
grammar.desc: suggest·apologise·recommend 현재형으로 발화 행위를 함
examples: I apologise for the delay.

grammar.key: SUBJECT AND OBJECT PRONOUNS, BOTH, A FEW, ANOTHER (both, a few, another)
grammar.en: Use both, a few or another as subject or object.
grammar.desc: both·a few·another를 주어·목적어로 사용함
examples: Both are ready, and I can carry both.

grammar.key: WITH OF + OBJECT PRONOUN (of, some, a few, any, each)
grammar.en: Use some, a few, any or each of an object pronoun.
grammar.desc: some·each 등 뒤 of와 목적격 대명사를 사용함
examples: Some of them are waiting outside.

grammar.en: Use each other for reciprocal actions.
grammar.desc: each other로 서로에게 하는 행동을 나타냄
examples: The neighbours help each other.

grammar.key: SINGULAR, AFTER PREPOSITIONS (myself, yourself, himself, herself)
grammar.en: Use a reflexive after a preposition for the same person.
grammar.desc: 전치사 목적어가 주어와 같으면 재귀대명사를 사용함
examples: She kept the money for herself.

grammar.key: SINGULAR, FOR EMPHASIS (myself, yourself, himself, herself)
grammar.en: Emphasize the actor with a singular reflexive.
grammar.desc: 단수 재귀대명사로 행위자를 강조함
examples: I repaired the bicycle myself.

grammar.key: BY + SINGULAR (by, myself, yourself, himself, herself)
grammar.en: Use by and a reflexive to mean without help.
grammar.desc: by와 재귀대명사로 도움 없이 혼자임을 나타냄
examples: He cooked dinner by himself.

grammar.en: Use whose name in a relative clause.
grammar.desc: 관계절 안에 whose name을 사용함
examples: The woman whose name is on the list is waiting.

grammar.en: Report a thought with wonder and a wh-clause.
grammar.desc: wonder 뒤 의문사절로 생각과 의문을 전달함
examples: I wondered where she had gone.

grammar.key: REPORTED STATEMENTS, PRONOUN AND TENSE SHIFT (say, tell, that-)
grammar.en: Shift pronouns and tense in say or tell reports.
grammar.desc: say·tell 간접화법에서 대명사와 시제를 조정함
examples: She told me that she had lost her keys.

grammar.key: REPORTED REQUESTS AND COMMANDS (ask, tell, to-)
grammar.en: Report requests with ask or tell, an object and to.
grammar.desc: ask·tell 뒤 목적어와 to부정사로 요청·명령을 전달함
examples: He asked me to close the window.

grammar.en: Use which one in an indirect question.
grammar.desc: 간접의문문에서 which one으로 선택 대상을 질문함
examples: I don't know which one to choose.

grammar.key: THIS ONE, THAT ONE (this one, that one)
grammar.en: Use this one or that one for a singular count noun.
grammar.desc: this one·that one으로 단수 가산 대상을 가리킴
examples: This one is smaller than that one.

grammar.key: AFFIRMATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + AFFIRMATIVE QUESTION TAGS
grammar.en: Add an affirmative tag to an affirmative clause.
grammar.desc: 긍정절 뒤 긍정 부가의문문을 덧붙임
examples: So you found the key, did you?

grammar.key: NEGATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + AFFIRMATIVE QUESTION TAGS (be, do, have)
grammar.en: Add an affirmative be, do or have tag to a negative clause.
grammar.desc: 부정절 뒤 be·do·have의 긍정 부가의문문을 사용함
examples: You haven't booked yet, have you?

grammar.en: Add right as an informal question tag.
grammar.desc: 비격식 발화 끝에 right로 확인 질문을 덧붙임
examples: You're coming tomorrow, right?

grammar.key: AFFIRMATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + NEGATIVE QUESTION TAGS (be, do, have)
grammar.en: Use negative tags with affirmative statements.
grammar.desc: 긍정 서술절 뒤 부정 부가의문문을 사용함
examples: You've finished, haven't you?

grammar.en: Use there is not or there are not with nouns.
grammar.desc: there be 부정형과 명사로 부재를 나타냄
examples: There aren't any empty seats.

grammar.key: SEMI-MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS, USED TO, OUGHT TO (used to, ought to)
grammar.en: Use semi-modals used to and ought to.
grammar.desc: 준조동사 used to·ought to를 사용함
examples: We used to live here, and we ought to visit again.

grammar.key: WITH DETERMINERS, QUANTITY (much, a bit of, a little bit of, enough, further, plenty of, loads of)
grammar.en: Use varied quantity expressions with mass nouns.
grammar.desc: 불가산 명사에 다양한 수량 표현을 사용함
examples: We need plenty of water.

grammar.en: Use used to for habits or states no longer true.
grammar.desc: used to로 지금은 달라진 과거 습관·상태를 나타냄
examples: I used to walk to work, but now I take the bus.

grammar.key: NEGATIVE (used to, didn, and, t used to)
grammar.en: Negate used to with didn't use to.
grammar.desc: didn't use to로 과거 습관을 부정함
examples: I didn't use to drink coffee.

grammar.en: Form affirmative used to statements.
grammar.desc: used to를 사용한 긍정절을 구성함
examples: She used to live in York.

grammar.en: Ask negative wh-questions with modal verbs.
grammar.desc: 법조동사 부정형으로 의문사 질문을 구성함
examples: Why can't we leave now?

grammar.en: Use will for dated or timetabled plans.
grammar.desc: will과 날짜·시각으로 확정된 미래 계획을 나타냄
examples: The train will depart at six tomorrow.

grammar.en: Use would for future events viewed from the past.
grammar.desc: would로 과거 시점에서 본 미래 일을 나타냄
examples: I knew she would arrive late.

grammar.en: Use wouldn't to express refusal in the past.
grammar.desc: wouldn't로 과거의 거부 의사를 나타냄
examples: He wouldn't tell me the answer.

grammar.key: POLITE REQUESTS (would, wouldn't, would you mind)
grammar.en: Make a polite request with Would you mind.
grammar.desc: Would you mind로 요청을 정중하게 제시함
examples: Would you mind closing the door?

grammar.key: INDIRECTNESS (would, wouldn't, advise, imagine, recommend, say)
grammar.en: Use would advise or recommend for indirect advice.
grammar.desc: would advise·recommend 등으로 조언의 직접성을 줄임
examples: I would recommend booking early.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (would, wouldn't, really, probably, certainly, definitely)
grammar.en: Place really or probably inside a would clause.
grammar.desc: would절에 really·probably 등 부사를 사용함
examples: I would probably choose the smaller room.

grammar.en: Backshift will to would in reported speech.
grammar.desc: 간접화법에서 will을 would로 전환함
examples: She said that she would call me.

grammar.en: Form affirmative would have clauses.
grammar.desc: would have 뒤 과거분사로 긍정절을 구성함
examples: I would have enjoyed that trip.

grammar.key: IMAGINED SITUATIONS IN THE PAST (would, wouldn't)
grammar.en: Describe an imagined past with would have.
grammar.desc: would have로 실제와 다른 과거 상황을 나타냄
examples: If you had asked, I would have helped.

grammar.en: Build questions using would.
grammar.desc: would를 사용한 의문문을 구성함
examples: What would you choose?

grammar.key: PAST NEGATIVE (would, wouldn't, would not have)
grammar.en: Use would not have or wouldn't have with a participle.
grammar.desc: wouldn't have와 과거분사로 부정절을 구성함
examples: I wouldn't have bought that car.

grammar.en: Use would in the result clause of a hypothetical if sentence.
grammar.desc: 가정하는 if문장의 결과절에 would를 사용함
examples: If I had more time, I would learn another language.

grammar.en: Use negative main-verb be in yes-no questions.
grammar.desc: 본동사 be 부정형으로 예·아니요 의문문을 구성함
examples: Aren't you tired?

grammar.en: Seek agreement with a negative yes-no question.
grammar.desc: 부정 예·아니요 의문문으로 동의를 구함
examples: Isn't this a lovely garden?

grammar.en: Use don't or haven't to start negative questions.
grammar.desc: do·have 부정형으로 부정 의문문을 구성함
examples: Haven't you sent the file?

grammar.en: Use a negative modal before the subject in a question.
grammar.desc: 주어 앞 법조동사 부정형으로 의문문을 구성함
examples: Can't you wait a moment?

grammar.key: THE MORE … THE MORE … (more, less, worse)
grammar.en: Link related changes with the more, the more.
grammar.desc: the more·the more 등으로 연동되는 변화를 나타냄
examples: The more I practise, the better I play.

grammar.key: GUESSES AND PREDICTIONS (can, cannot, can't, and)
grammar.en: Draw negative deductions with can't or cannot.
grammar.desc: can't·cannot으로 불가능하다는 추측을 나타냄
examples: That can't be Mia; she is abroad.

grammar.key: GENERAL TRUTHS AND TENDENCIES (can, cannot, can't)
grammar.en: Use can for general truths and tendencies.
grammar.desc: can으로 일반적인 사실과 경향을 나타냄
examples: Large cities can be noisy.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (can, cannot, can't, easily, hardly, now, probably, sometimes, still)
grammar.en: Use varied mid-position adverbs with can.
grammar.desc: can과 다양한 중간 위치 부사를 함께 사용함
examples: You can easily find the station.

grammar.en: Follow a superlative with a clause for uniqueness.
grammar.desc: 최상급 뒤 절로 특별한 대상을 비교함
examples: It was the nicest room that we saw.

grammar.en: Put much before an attributive comparative adjective.
grammar.desc: 명사 앞 비교급 형용사를 much로 강조함
examples: We need a much larger table.

grammar.en: Intensify a predicative comparative with a lot.
grammar.desc: 보어 비교급 앞 a lot으로 차이를 강조함
examples: This room is a lot warmer.

grammar.en: Use varied non-finite comparison clauses after than.
grammar.desc: than 뒤 다양한 비정형절로 비교 대상을 제시함
examples: It is safer to wait than to drive through the flood.

grammar.en: Use dare not or daren't before a bare infinitive.
grammar.desc: dare not·daren't 뒤 동사 원형으로 부정함
examples: I daren't open the door.

grammar.en: Use affirmative semi-modal dare with a bare infinitive.
grammar.desc: 준조동사 dare 긍정형 뒤 동사 원형을 사용함
examples: I dare say he will agree.

grammar.en: Use semi-modal dare to describe courage to act.
grammar.desc: 준조동사 dare로 행동할 용기를 나타냄
examples: I dare face the challenge alone.

grammar.key: BE SURE/CERTAIN TO (be sure, certain to, be sure to, be certain to)
grammar.en: Express certainty with be sure or certain to.
grammar.desc: be sure·certain to로 확실함을 나타냄
examples: She is certain to arrive soon.

grammar.key: BE BOUND TO, CERTAINTY (be bound to, be, bound to)
grammar.en: Express inevitability with be bound to.
grammar.desc: be bound to로 반드시 일어날 일을 나타냄
examples: This plan is bound to succeed.

grammar.key: BE MORE/LESS LIKELY, COMPARISON (be more, less likely, less, likely)
grammar.en: Compare probability with more or less likely.
grammar.desc: more·less likely로 가능성의 정도를 비교함
examples: They are less likely to arrive late.

grammar.key: BE EXPRESSIONS + INFINITIVE (be, be likely to, be due to, be meant to, be bound to, be sure to, be certain to, be obliged to, will)
grammar.en: Use varied be plus infinitive modal expressions.
grammar.desc: be likely to 등 다양한 be 부정사 표현을 사용함
examples: The train is due to arrive at six.

grammar.key: BE FORCED TO, OBLIGATION (be forced to)
grammar.en: Describe an unavoidable obligation with be forced to.
grammar.desc: be forced to로 상황이 강요하는 의무를 나타냄
examples: We were forced to cancel the trip.

grammar.key: BE LIKELY TO, PROBABILITY (be likely to, be, likely to)
grammar.en: Express probability with be likely to.
grammar.desc: be likely to로 일어날 가능성을 나타냄
examples: The road is likely to be busy.

grammar.en: Ask yes-no and wh-questions in future continuous.
grammar.desc: 미래진행형으로 예·아니요 질문과 의문사 질문을 구성함
examples: When will you be returning?

grammar.key: IMMEDIATE FUTURE WITH BE ABOUT TO (be about to, just)
grammar.en: Describe the immediate future with be about to.
grammar.desc: be about to로 곧 일어날 일을 나타냄
examples: I'm just about to leave.

grammar.key: BE ABOUT TO (be about to, be, about to, just)
grammar.en: Use was about to for an imminent event in the past.
grammar.desc: was·were about to로 과거 시점의 임박한 일을 나타냄
examples: I was about to leave when you called.

grammar.en: Negate future perfect continuous with will not have been.
grammar.desc: will not have been과 ing형으로 미래완료진행형을 부정함
examples: By noon, I will not have been waiting for an hour.

grammar.en: Negate future perfect simple with will not have.
grammar.desc: will not have와 과거분사로 미래완료형을 부정함
examples: I will not have finished the report by Friday.

grammar.key: SUGGESTION (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Make a strong recommendation with you've got to.
grammar.desc: you've got to로 강한 권유를 나타냄
examples: You've got to try this soup.

grammar.en: Suggest avoiding an action with let's not.
grammar.desc: let's not 뒤 동사 원형으로 행동을 피하도록 제안함
examples: Let's not argue about the price.

grammar.en: Put a mid-position adverb in a negative question.
grammar.desc: 부정 의문문의 주어와 본동사 사이에 부사를 사용함
examples: Don't you usually work on Mondays?

grammar.key: FOCUSING (may, you may know, as you may have)
grammar.en: Refer to shared knowledge with as you may know.
grammar.desc: as you may know 등으로 공유 지식을 환기함
examples: As you may know, the office is moving.

grammar.en: Offer a contrasting view with may followed by but.
grammar.desc: may절 뒤 but절로 예상과 다른 관점을 제시함
examples: The room may be small, but it is comfortable.

grammar.en: Request permission politely with May I.
grammar.desc: May I로 허락을 정중하게 요청함
examples: May I borrow your pen?

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (may, even, only, already, never, just, sometimes)
grammar.en: Use varied mid-position adverbs after may.
grammar.desc: may 뒤 중간 위치에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: The parcel may already be here.

grammar.en: Give a formal request or suggestion with May I.
grammar.desc: 격식 발화에서 May I로 요청·제안을 제시함
examples: May I suggest that we begin now?

grammar.en: Express past possibility with may have and a participle.
grammar.desc: may have와 과거분사로 과거의 가능성을 나타냄
examples: She may have missed the train.

grammar.en: Follow adjective enough with a to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: 형용사 enough 뒤 to부정사로 충분한 정도를 나타냄
examples: The hall is large enough to hold everyone.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (must, mustn't, all, never, strongly, first)
grammar.en: Use varied mid-position adverbs after must.
grammar.desc: must 뒤 중간 위치에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: You must first read the instructions.

grammar.key: CONCESSIONS (must, mustn't, i must admit, you must admit)
grammar.en: Concede a point with I must admit or you must admit.
grammar.desc: I·you must admit으로 양보하며 내용을 인정함
examples: I must admit that your plan is better.

grammar.en: Use negative must forms to state rules of prohibition.
grammar.desc: must 부정형으로 허용되지 않는 규칙을 나타냄
examples: Visitors must not enter this room.

grammar.en: Form affirmative must have clauses.
grammar.desc: must have 뒤 과거분사로 긍정절을 구성함
examples: She must have left already.

grammar.en: Infer a past event with must have and a participle.
grammar.desc: must have와 과거분사로 과거 사건을 추론함
examples: The floor is wet; someone must have washed it.

grammar.en: Use need not or needn't before a bare infinitive.
grammar.desc: need not·needn't와 동사 원형으로 필요를 부정함
examples: You needn't wait for me.

grammar.key: NEVER, INVERTED FRONT POSITION, FOCUS (never, i)
grammar.en: Front never and invert auxiliary and subject.
grammar.desc: never를 문두에 놓고 주어·조동사를 도치하여 강조함
examples: Never have I seen such a quiet street.

grammar.key: NEITHER OF, NONE OF + PRONOUN (neither of, none of)
grammar.en: Use neither of or none of with an affirmative verb.
grammar.desc: neither of·none of와 긍정 동사로 전체를 부정함
examples: Neither of them knows the answer.

grammar.key: NOUN + OF + POSSESSIVE DETERMINER + NOUN (of, friend, friends)
grammar.en: Use noun of possessive noun phrases for relationships.
grammar.desc: 명사 of 뒤 소유 명사구로 관계를 나타냄
examples: A friend of my sister's is visiting.

grammar.en: Use ought to for desired states of affairs.
grammar.desc: ought to로 바람직한 상태를 나타냄
examples: Everyone ought to have clean drinking water.

grammar.en: Use affirmative or negative passive infinitives.
grammar.desc: 다양한 구문에서 긍정·부정 수동 부정사를 사용함
examples: It is important to be prepared.

grammar.en: Use modal have been with a past participle.
grammar.desc: 조동사 have been과 과거분사로 과거 수동을 나타냄
examples: The parcel may have been delivered already.

grammar.en: Use had been with a participle in affirmative passive clauses.
grammar.desc: had been과 과거분사로 긍정 과거완료 수동태를 만듦
examples: The room had been cleaned before we arrived.

grammar.en: Use was or were being with a past participle.
grammar.desc: was·were being과 과거분사로 과거진행 수동태를 만듦
examples: The road was being repaired when we passed.

grammar.en: Use had not been with a participle in passive clauses.
grammar.desc: had not been과 과거분사로 과거완료 수동태를 부정함
examples: The tickets had not been printed when we arrived.

grammar.en: Use will be with a participle for future passive events.
grammar.desc: will be와 과거분사로 미래 수동 사건을 나타냄
examples: The results will be announced tomorrow.

grammar.en: Use mid-position adverbs in past perfect continuous.
grammar.desc: 과거완료진행형의 중간 위치에 부사를 사용함
examples: She had been quietly working for an hour.

grammar.en: Use past perfect continuous after a time conjunction.
grammar.desc: 시간 접속사 뒤 과거완료진행형으로 배경을 나타냄
examples: After she had been waiting for an hour, the bus arrived.

grammar.key: AFTER IF ONLY AND WISH, IMAGINED PAST (if only, wish)
grammar.en: Use if only or wish with past perfect for regret.
grammar.desc: if only·wish 뒤 과거완료로 과거의 후회를 나타냄
examples: I wish I had booked earlier.

grammar.key: POLITENESS: I WONDERED AND I WANTED (i wondered, i wanted)
grammar.en: Make a request indirect with I wondered or I wanted.
grammar.desc: I wondered·I wanted 과거형으로 정중하게 요청함
examples: I wondered if you could send me the details.

grammar.key: FRONT POSITION, INVERSION WITH NEVER (never, i)
grammar.en: Use fronted never with inversion for emphasis.
grammar.desc: 문두 never와 도치로 경험의 부재를 강조함
examples: Never had I felt so relieved.

grammar.key: DEGREE ADJECTIVES BEFORE NOUNS (real, absolute, complete)
grammar.en: Put real, absolute or complete before a noun.
grammar.desc: 명사 앞 real·absolute·complete로 의미를 강조함
examples: The journey was a complete success.

grammar.en: Use present, future or former attributively.
grammar.desc: present·future·former를 명사 앞 수식어로 사용함
examples: Her former colleague lives nearby.

grammar.en: Use ours after noun plus of.
grammar.desc: 명사 of 뒤 ours로 소유 관계를 나타냄
examples: A colleague of ours is visiting.

grammar.en: Use its before a noun for singular nonhuman possession.
grammar.desc: 단수 비인간 대상의 소유에 its를 사용함
examples: The machine has lost its power supply.

grammar.en: Add possessive 's to a noun phrase containing of.
grammar.desc: of를 포함한 명사구 끝에 's로 소유를 나타냄
examples: The manager of the shop's office is upstairs.

grammar.en: Use their for a singular generic person or group.
grammar.desc: 단수로 표현한 일반적 사람·집단의 소유에 their를 사용함
examples: Every student should bring their notebook.

grammar.en: Ask about future plans with many continuous verbs.
