grammar.desc: 다양한 현재진행형 동사로 미래 계획을 질문함
examples: Are you presenting your report tomorrow?

grammar.en: Describe future arrangements with many continuous verbs.
grammar.desc: 다양한 현재진행형 동사로 미래 일정을 나타냄
examples: We are attending the workshop next Friday.

grammar.en: Use present perfect continuous for recent visible effects.
grammar.desc: 현재완료진행형으로 최근 활동의 현재 영향을 나타냄
examples: Your hands are dirty. Have you been gardening?

grammar.en: Put still before a negative present-perfect expression.
grammar.desc: 현재완료 부정형 앞 still로 계속된 미완료를 강조함
examples: She still hasn't replied.

grammar.en: Use varied present-simple verbs to perform speech acts.
grammar.desc: accept·advise 등 다양한 현재형으로 발화 행위를 함
examples: I accept your offer.

grammar.en: Modify little and few to express insufficient quantity.
grammar.desc: little·few 앞 수식어로 부족한 수량을 나타냄
examples: We have very little time and very few seats.

grammar.en: Use one another for reciprocity in formal contexts.
grammar.desc: 격식 맥락에서 one another로 상호 행동을 나타냄
examples: The committee members support one another.

grammar.en: Intensify a description with in itself.
grammar.desc: in itself로 그 자체의 속성을 강조함
examples: The idea is useful in itself.

grammar.en: Use help yourselves to politely invite several people to take food or drinks.
grammar.desc: help yourselves to로 여러 청자에게 음식이나 음료를 정중히 권유함
examples: Please help yourselves to some tea.

grammar.en: Add a non-defining whose clause for extra information.
grammar.desc: 비제한적 whose 관계절로 부가 정보를 제시함
examples: My neighbour, whose car broke down, took the bus.

grammar.en: Strand a preposition at the end of a relative clause.
grammar.desc: 관계절 끝에 전치사를 남겨 관계대명사와 연결함
examples: The chair which I sat on was uncomfortable.

grammar.en: Use a defining whose clause to describe a relationship.
grammar.desc: 제한적 whose 관계절로 소유·관계를 나타냄
examples: The student whose bag was missing called us.

grammar.en: Evaluate a whole statement in a following relative clause.
grammar.desc: 앞선 절 전체를 관계절로 받아 평가함
examples: She finished early, which was very helpful.

grammar.en: Use should be followed by an -ing form.
grammar.desc: should be 뒤 ing형으로 진행형을 구성함
examples: You should be resting now.

grammar.en: Express an expected ongoing act with should be -ing.
grammar.desc: should be ing형으로 예상되는 진행 동작을 나타냄
examples: They should be arriving about now.

grammar.en: Express a current duty with should be -ing.
grammar.desc: should be ing형으로 현재 해야 하는 행동을 나타냄
examples: You should be studying instead of watching videos.

grammar.en: Add information with an initial -ing clause.
grammar.desc: 문두 ing 비정형절로 추가 정보를 제시함
examples: Walking along the path, I noticed a small bridge.

grammar.en: Use a finite subordinate clause to state a condition.
grammar.desc: 정형 종속절로 조건을 제시함
examples: Provided that you finish early, you can leave.

grammar.en: Use after having or being and a participle for past time.
grammar.desc: after having·being과 과거분사로 앞선 시간을 나타냄
examples: After having checked the list, she sent the invitations.

grammar.en: Use would for repeated past actions.
grammar.desc: would로 과거의 반복적인 행동을 나타냄
examples: Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.

grammar.en: Use compounds such as up-to-date or state-of-the-art.
grammar.desc: up-to-date 등 다양한 합성 형용사를 사용함
examples: The hospital has state-of-the-art equipment.

grammar.key: THE SAME (+ NOUN) + AS + CLAUSE (the same, as)
grammar.en: Compare identity with the same as followed by a clause.
grammar.desc: the same as 뒤 절로 동일성을 비교함
examples: I ordered the same dish as you did.

grammar.en: Modify a comparative with slightly for a small difference.
grammar.desc: slightly로 비교급의 차이가 작음을 나타냄
examples: This route is slightly shorter.

grammar.en: Use adjective enough to before a verb.
grammar.desc: 형용사 enough to로 행동하기에 충분함을 나타냄
examples: The bag is light enough to carry.

grammar.en: Compare alternatives with rather than and a non-finite clause.
grammar.desc: rather than 뒤 비정형절로 선택을 비교함
examples: I chose to walk rather than wait for the bus.

grammar.key: AS IF OR AS THOUGH + FINITE CLAUSE (as if, as though)
grammar.en: Compare situations with as if or as though and a clause.
grammar.desc: as if·as though 뒤 절로 상황을 비교함
examples: She looked as if she had seen a ghost.

grammar.en: Focus coordinated clauses with not only but also.
grammar.desc: not only·but also로 절을 연결하여 강조함
examples: She not only cooked dinner but also washed the dishes.

grammar.en: Coordinate negative alternatives with neither nor.
grammar.desc: neither·nor로 절을 연결하여 양쪽을 부정함
examples: She neither called us nor sent a message.

grammar.en: Speculate about the past with could have.
grammar.desc: could have와 과거분사로 과거를 추측함
examples: He could have taken the earlier train.

grammar.en: Use could have followed by a past participle.
grammar.desc: could have 뒤 과거분사로 절을 구성함
examples: We could have finished sooner.

grammar.en: Shift can to could in reported speech.
grammar.desc: 간접화법에서 can을 could로 전환함
examples: She said that she could help.

grammar.en: Express regret about a missed option with could have.
grammar.desc: could have로 실행하지 않은 행동을 후회함
examples: I could have called you, but I forgot.

grammar.en: Use affirmative could have for a past possibility.
grammar.desc: could have 긍정형으로 과거의 가능성을 나타냄
examples: The delay could have caused a serious problem.

grammar.en: Substitute those followed by a relative or participle clause.
grammar.desc: those 뒤 관계절·분사절로 특정 대상을 나타냄
examples: Those waiting outside can come in now.

grammar.key: BE DUE TO, BE TO, SCHEDULES (be due to, be to)
grammar.en: Use be due to or formal be to for schedules.
grammar.desc: be due to·be to로 예정된 일정을 나타냄
examples: The minister is to visit on Friday.

grammar.key: BE DUE TO (be due to, be, due to) (B4)
grammar.en: Use present be due to before a verb.
grammar.desc: 현재형 be due to 뒤 동사로 예정된 일을 나타냄
examples: The train is due to arrive at six.
grammar.surface: BE DUE TO (be due to, be, due to)

grammar.en: Use present be to before a verb for a formal schedule.
grammar.desc: 현재형 be to 뒤 동사로 공식 일정을 나타냄
examples: The committee is to meet tomorrow.

grammar.en: Form affirmative future-perfect clauses with will.
grammar.desc: will have와 과거분사로 긍정 미래완료절을 구성함
examples: By Friday, I will have finished the report.

grammar.en: Use they or them for gender-unspecified antecedents.
grammar.desc: 성별·수를 특정하지 않은 선행사를 they·them으로 받음
examples: If someone calls, ask them to wait.

grammar.en: Use we or us for people in general.
grammar.desc: we·us로 일반적인 사람들을 가리킴
examples: We all need time to rest.

grammar.en: Use have, an object and a participle for a caused service.
grammar.desc: have 뒤 목적어와 과거분사로 서비스·경험을 나타냄
examples: I had my bicycle repaired yesterday.

grammar.en: Put a reflexive inside a get-passive construction.
grammar.desc: get 수동구문에 재귀대명사를 사용함
examples: He got himself locked out.

grammar.en: Cause an action with get, an object and a to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: get 뒤 목적어와 to부정사로 행동을 유도함
examples: I got my brother to help me.

grammar.en: Use full do not in a formal or emphatic command.
grammar.desc: 격식·강조 명령문에 축약하지 않은 do not을 사용함
examples: Do not enter this room.

grammar.en: Use rather a before an adjective and noun.
grammar.desc: rather a 뒤 형용사와 명사로 정도를 나타냄
examples: It was rather a difficult journey.

grammar.en: Form a question with must before the subject.
grammar.desc: must를 주어 앞에 놓아 의문문을 구성함
examples: Must we book in advance?

grammar.en: Negate past-simple passive clauses.
grammar.desc: 단순과거 수동태 부정절을 구성함
examples: The windows were not repaired yesterday.

grammar.en: Use modal verbs with passive be and a participle.
grammar.desc: 법조동사 뒤 be와 과거분사로 수동태를 구성함
examples: These tickets must be checked.

grammar.en: Use varied verbs in present-continuous passive clauses.
grammar.desc: 다양한 동사를 현재진행 수동태로 사용함
examples: The documents are being translated.

grammar.en: Use have been with a participle in an affirmative passive.
grammar.desc: have been과 과거분사로 긍정 현재완료 수동태를 만듦
examples: The results have been published.

grammar.en: Use have not been with a participle in a negative passive.
grammar.desc: have not been과 과거분사로 현재완료 수동태를 부정함
examples: The results have not been published.

grammar.key: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS, , WITH PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE
grammar.en: Make a direct object the passive subject and retain a prepositional recipient.
grammar.desc: 직접목적어를 수동 주어로 삼고 수혜자를 전치사구로 나타냄
examples: A ticket was given to each visitor.

grammar.en: Summarize or evaluate with a modal passive.
grammar.desc: 조동사 수동태로 내용을 요약하거나 평가함
examples: The trial can be considered a success.

grammar.en: Use an indirect object as passive subject with varied verbs.
grammar.desc: 다양한 동사의 간접목적어를 수동태 주어로 사용함
examples: She has been offered a new job.

grammar.en: Negate present-continuous passive clauses.
grammar.desc: 현재진행 수동태 부정절을 구성함
examples: The bridge is not being repaired today.

grammar.en: Use a broad range of adverbs in past continuous.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형의 중간 위치에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: She was steadily improving her skills.

grammar.en: Build negative past-perfect-continuous clauses.
grammar.desc: 과거완료진행형 부정절을 구성함
examples: They had not been waiting long when I arrived.

grammar.en: Give background in a past-perfect-continuous relative clause.
grammar.desc: 관계절의 과거완료진행형으로 배경 정보를 나타냄
examples: The woman who had been waiting outside finally came in.

grammar.en: Front never before and invert a past-perfect clause.
grammar.desc: never before 뒤 과거완료절을 도치하여 강조함
examples: Never before had I seen such a quiet street.

grammar.en: Use inverted no sooner had followed by than.
grammar.desc: No sooner had 도치와 than으로 직후 사건을 나타냄
examples: No sooner had we arrived than the rain began.

grammar.en: Use past perfect to describe a changed situation.
grammar.desc: 과거완료로 이전과 달라진 상황을 나타냄
examples: The room was empty; everyone had gone home.

grammar.en: Use past perfect after because for an explanation.
grammar.desc: because 뒤 과거완료로 앞선 이유를 설명함
examples: I couldn't open the door because I had lost the key.

grammar.en: Use varied mid-position adverbs in past perfect.
grammar.desc: 과거완료절 중간에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: She had recently moved to a new flat.

grammar.en: Form questions in the past perfect.
grammar.desc: 과거완료 의문문을 구성함
examples: Had you finished before she arrived?

grammar.en: Use past perfect in a background relative clause.
grammar.desc: 관계절의 과거완료로 배경 정보를 나타냄
examples: The book that I had borrowed was missing.

grammar.en: Report a statement with past perfect after a past verb.
grammar.desc: 과거 보고동사 뒤 과거완료로 서술을 전달함
examples: She said that she had finished the report.

grammar.en: Report a question with past perfect after a past verb.
grammar.desc: 과거 보고동사 뒤 과거완료로 질문을 전달함
examples: He asked whether I had booked a seat.

grammar.en: Add varied time adjuncts to past-simple statements.
grammar.desc: 단순과거에 다양한 시간 부가어를 사용함
examples: We moved here three years ago.

grammar.key: WITH SUBORDINATING CONJUNCTIONS (as soon as, before, if, once, since, so, until, when, while)
grammar.en: Use past simple after varied subordinating conjunctions.
grammar.desc: 다양한 종속접속사 뒤 단순과거를 사용함
examples: As soon as she arrived, we started dinner.

grammar.en: Use past simple in an if-clause to make a polite request.
grammar.desc: if절의 과거형으로 요청의 직접성을 줄임
examples: I would appreciate it if you sent the details today.

grammar.key: COMPARATIVE CLAUSES WITH OURS, HERS (ours, hers)
grammar.en: Use ours or hers in comparative clauses.
grammar.desc: 비교절에서 소유대명사 ours·hers를 사용함
examples: Their room is larger than ours.

grammar.en: Use theirs as an object or complement.
grammar.desc: theirs를 소유 대상의 목적어·보어로 사용함
examples: Our car broke down, so we borrowed theirs.

grammar.en: Use ours as an object or complement.
grammar.desc: ours를 소유 대상의 목적어·보어로 사용함
examples: They used our tools, and then they returned ours.

grammar.en: Use hers as an object or complement.
grammar.desc: hers를 소유 대상의 목적어·보어로 사용함
examples: I forgot my coat, so I borrowed hers.

grammar.en: Use frequency adverbs with continuous for striking habits.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형과 빈도 부사로 두드러진 습관을 나타냄
examples: He is constantly asking the same question.

grammar.key: INVERSION WITH NOT ONLY ? BUT ALSO (do) (B4)
grammar.en: Front not only and invert auxiliary do for focus.
grammar.desc: 문두 not only 뒤 조동사 do를 도치하여 강조함
examples: Not only does she teach, but she also writes books.
grammar.surface: INVERSION WITH NOT ONLY ? BUT ALSO (do)

grammar.en: Use present simple to summarize a plot dramatically.
grammar.desc: 현재형으로 줄거리와 역사 사건을 생생하게 요약함
examples: The hero opens the door and discovers the missing letter.

grammar.key: WITH OF + OBJECT PRONOUN (of, neither, either, none)
grammar.en: Use neither, either or none of an object pronoun.
grammar.desc: neither·either·none of 뒤 목적격 대명사를 사용함
examples: Neither of them was ready.

grammar.key: SUBJECT AND OBJECT PRONOUNS, EACH, SEVERAL, NEITHER, ENOUGH (each, several, neither, enough, either)
grammar.en: Use each, either, neither or several as pronouns.
grammar.desc: each·either·neither·several 등을 대명사로 사용함
examples: Several arrived early, and I greeted each.

grammar.en: Use by with a plural reflexive for acting without help.
grammar.desc: by와 복수 재귀대명사로 도움 없이 행동함을 나타냄
examples: We built the table by ourselves.

grammar.en: Emphasize the entity with itself.
grammar.desc: itself로 해당 대상 자체를 강조함
examples: The building itself is quite old.

grammar.en: Use by itself for acting alone or without assistance.
grammar.desc: by itself로 홀로 또는 도움 없이 작동함을 나타냄
examples: The door opened by itself.

grammar.key: REPORTED REQUESTS AND COMMANDS, NEGATIVE (ask, tell, not, to-)
grammar.en: Report a negative command with tell and not to.
grammar.desc: ask·tell 뒤 목적어와 not to로 부정 지시를 전달함
examples: She told me not to open the window.

grammar.en: Use generic one as subject for people in general.
grammar.desc: one을 일반적인 사람을 가리키는 주어로 사용함
examples: One should always check the instructions.

grammar.en: Use anticipatory it after make before a later clause.
grammar.desc: make 뒤 가목적어 it으로 뒤의 내용을 예고함
examples: I made it clear that I would not attend.

grammar.key: (SUBJECT) EMPTY IT (it, appears, feels, looks, seems)
grammar.en: Use dummy it with appears, feels, looks or seems.
grammar.desc: appears·feels·looks·seems 앞 가주어 it을 사용함
examples: It seems that the bus is late.

grammar.en: Strengthen a superlative with by far.
grammar.desc: 최상급 앞 by far로 차이의 정도를 강조함
examples: This is by far the quietest room.

grammar.en: Soften an imperative with a following question tag.
grammar.desc: 명령문 뒤 부가의문문으로 직접성을 줄임
examples: Take a seat, won't you?

grammar.key: SEMI-MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS, DARE, NEED (dare, need)
grammar.en: Use dare and need as semi-modal auxiliaries.
grammar.desc: dare·need를 준조동사로 사용함
examples: You needn't worry, and you daren't ignore the warning.

grammar.en: Use a wh-word with negative auxiliary do.
grammar.desc: 의문사와 do 부정형으로 일반동사 질문을 구성함
examples: Why didn't you tell me?

grammar.en: Put enough after an adverb to mark sufficient degree.
grammar.desc: 부사 뒤 enough로 충분한 정도를 나타냄
examples: She spoke clearly enough to be understood.

grammar.en: Use a broad range of adverbs after can.
grammar.desc: can 뒤 중간 위치에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: You can undoubtedly improve with practice.

grammar.key: PASSIVE (can, cannot, can't, it can be said that, it can be considered)
grammar.en: Use can in impersonal passive reporting clauses.
grammar.desc: 격식 보고문에서 can을 비인칭 수동절에 사용함
examples: It can be concluded that the plan worked.

grammar.key: SUPERLATIVE ADVERB BEST + CLAUSE (best, the best, can, could)
grammar.en: Use the best before an ellipted can or could clause.
grammar.desc: the best 부사 뒤 can·could 생략절을 사용함
examples: I did the best I could.

grammar.key: IF + PAST PERFECT + MODAL VERBS IMAGINED SITUATION, REGRET (if, have)
grammar.en: Use past if and modal have clauses for imagined history.
grammar.desc: 과거완료 if절과 조동사 have로 가상 과거를 나타냄
examples: If we had left earlier, we might have caught the bus.

grammar.en: Connect an unexpected contrast with and yet.
grammar.desc: and yet으로 예상과 다른 대조를 연결함
examples: The room was small, and yet it felt comfortable.

grammar.en: Use varied certainty adverbs inside be going to.
grammar.desc: be going to의 중간 위치에 확실성 부사를 사용함
examples: She is certainly going to succeed.

grammar.en: Use get with an object and -ing for causation.
grammar.desc: get 뒤 목적어와 ing형으로 행동을 유도함
examples: The music got everyone dancing.

grammar.en: Use get with an object and participle for a service.
grammar.desc: get 뒤 목적어와 과거분사로 일을 맡기거나 시킴
examples: I got my bicycle repaired yesterday.

grammar.en: Give a condition with an imperative followed by and.
grammar.desc: 명령문 뒤 and로 조건과 그 결과를 연결함
examples: Follow this path, and you will reach the lake.

grammar.en: Use an imperative to direct attention to a document.
grammar.desc: 격식 문서에서 명령문으로 자료의 위치를 안내함
examples: See Table 2 for the complete results.

grammar.key: LET + THIRD PERSON PRONOUN, PERMISSION, ORDER (let, him, her, them)
grammar.en: Use let him, her or them to grant permission.
grammar.desc: let him·her·them 뒤 동사 원형으로 허용함
examples: Let them enter the room.

grammar.key: DONT LET + PRONOUN, PERMISSION, ORDER (let, him, her, them)
grammar.en: Use don't let with a pronoun to deny permission.
grammar.desc: don't let 뒤 대명사와 동사 원형으로 허용을 막음
examples: Don't let him touch the equipment.

grammar.en: Use anything in a contextually ellipted clause.
grammar.desc: 문맥상 생략된 절에서 anything을 사용함
examples: Anything I can do to help?

grammar.en: Use postmodified anything as a singular subject.
grammar.desc: 후치수식한 anything을 단수 주어로 사용함
examples: Anything you need is on the table.

grammar.en: Emphasize a possible unexpected result with may well.
grammar.desc: may well로 예상 밖의 가능성을 강조함
examples: The new rules may well surprise you.

grammar.key: POSSIBILITY IN THE PAST (might, might not have)
grammar.en: Use might not have for a possible negative past event.
grammar.desc: might not have로 과거의 부정 가능성을 나타냄
examples: She might not have received the letter.

grammar.en: Concede with might before a reassuring but clause.
grammar.desc: might절 뒤 but절로 위로나 정당화 내용을 제시함
examples: The room might be small, but at least it is warm.

grammar.key: WITH EXTREME ADVERBS (absolutely, extremely, incredibly, totally)
grammar.en: Intensify adjectives with extreme degree adverbs.
grammar.desc: extremely·incredibly 등 강한 정도 부사로 형용사를 강조함
examples: The journey was incredibly difficult.

grammar.en: Invert had and the subject for an imagined past.
grammar.desc: 과거 가정절에서 had와 주어를 도치함
examples: Had I known, I would have called you.

grammar.key: INVERSION WITH NOT ONLY ? BUT ALSO (do) (C1)
grammar.en: Front not only did before a contrasting but also clause.
grammar.desc: Not only did 도치와 but also로 과거 사건을 강조함
examples: Not only did she cook dinner, but she also washed the dishes.
grammar.surface: INVERSION WITH NOT ONLY ? BUT ALSO (do)

grammar.en: Use did before a base-form verb for past emphasis.
grammar.desc: did 뒤 동사 원형으로 과거 일을 강조함
examples: I did send the message yesterday.

grammar.en: Use varied past-simple question and tag forms.
grammar.desc: 다양한 과거형 질문과 부가의문문을 구성함
examples: Didn't you recognise the driver?

grammar.en: Make an idea indirect with past-simple I thought.
grammar.desc: I thought 과거형으로 의견의 직접성을 줄임
examples: I thought we could meet after lunch.

grammar.en: Use one's for generic possession.
grammar.desc: one's로 일반적인 사람의 소유를 나타냄
examples: One's health should come first.

grammar.key: EITHER, NEITHER WITH SINGULAR NOUNS (either, neither)
grammar.en: Use either or neither before a singular noun.
grammar.desc: 단수 명사 앞 either·neither를 사용함
examples: Neither option is suitable.

grammar.en: Use each as subject with the other as preposition complement.
grammar.desc: each 주어와 전치사 뒤 the other로 상호 관계를 나타냄
examples: Each room is connected to the other by a narrow door.

grammar.en: Give a highly formal command with shall.
grammar.desc: shall로 격식이 높은 명령을 제시함
examples: Applicants shall submit the form before Friday.

grammar.en: Use should inside an if-clause for a future possibility.
grammar.desc: if절 안 should로 미래의 가능 조건을 나타냄
examples: If you should need help, please call us.

grammar.en: Use an initial participle clause to foreground information.
grammar.desc: 문두 과거분사 비정형절로 정보를 부각함
examples: Written in plain language, the guide is easy to follow.

grammar.en: Use not followed by an -ing clause for extra information.
grammar.desc: not 뒤 ing 비정형절로 부정 배경 정보를 추가함
examples: Not knowing the address, I asked for directions.

grammar.en: Use a non-finite clause after if.
grammar.desc: if 뒤 비정형절로 조건을 제시함
examples: If needed, we can send another copy.

grammar.key: WITH POSTMODFIER AND NOUN (possible, ever, by far)
grammar.en: Strengthen a superlative noun phrase with a postmodifier.
grammar.desc: 최상급 명사구 뒤 possible·ever 등으로 강조함
examples: We chose the quietest room possible.

grammar.en: Use will to describe typical or habitual behavior.
grammar.desc: will로 전형적이거나 습관적인 행동을 나타냄
examples: On summer evenings, he will sit outside for hours.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (would, wouldn't, strongly, easily, especially, actually, absolutely, gladly)
grammar.en: Use increasingly varied adverbs with would.
grammar.desc: would와 다양한 부사를 함께 사용함
examples: I would gladly help you.

grammar.en: Ask an extreme alternative question for rhetorical force.
grammar.desc: 극단적인 대안 질문으로 발화의 효과를 높임
examples: Are you going to help, or are you going to stand there all day?

grammar.en: Hedge an alternative question by omitting its second modal.
grammar.desc: 선택 의문문의 두 번째 조동사를 생략하여 완곡하게 질문함
examples: Could we meet tomorrow, or perhaps wait until Friday?

grammar.key: PAST NEGATIVE, DEDUCTIONS (can, cannot, can't, or)
grammar.en: Use can't have with a participle for a past deduction.
grammar.desc: can't have와 과거분사로 과거의 불가능을 추론함
examples: She can't have written this; she was away.

grammar.en: Start a formal conditional clause with inverted should.
grammar.desc: 조건절 문두 should와 도치로 격식 조건을 나타냄
examples: Should you need assistance, please call us.

grammar.en: Use if with a past participle in an abbreviated clause.
grammar.desc: if 뒤 과거분사로 축약한 조건절을 구성함
examples: If invited, I will attend.

grammar.key: IF + SHOULD, FORMAL, POLITE (if, should, if you should)
grammar.en: Use if you should in polite formal conditionals.
grammar.desc: 격식 조건절에 if you should로 정중하게 제시함
examples: If you should need further details, please contact us.

grammar.key: NOT ONLY … BUT (ALSO) WITH INVERSION, FOCUS (not only)
grammar.en: Front not only with inversion before but also.
grammar.desc: not only 문두 도치와 but also로 절을 강조함
examples: Not only is the room cheap, but it is also near the station.

grammar.en: Use could have to criticize a missed action.
grammar.desc: could have로 실행하지 않은 행동을 비판함
examples: You could have warned me about the delay.

grammar.en: Form questions with semi-modal dare.
grammar.desc: 준조동사 dare 의문문을 구성함
examples: Dare you tell him the truth?

grammar.key: I DARE SAY (dare, i dare say)
grammar.en: Express probable truth with I dare say.
grammar.desc: I dare say로 아마 사실일 것이라는 판단을 나타냄
examples: I dare say she will arrive soon.

grammar.key: THAT OF, THOSE OF (that of, those of)
grammar.en: Substitute that of or those of for a possessive noun phrase.
grammar.desc: that of·those of로 소유 명사구를 대신함
examples: The new design resembles that of the old model.

grammar.en: Negate shall with shall not.
grammar.desc: shall not으로 부정절을 구성함
examples: We shall not forget this day.

grammar.en: Use a might question for polite criticism or suggestion.
grammar.desc: might 의문문으로 정중하게 비판하거나 제안함
examples: Might you not have checked the details first?

grammar.en: Form negative might not have clauses.
grammar.desc: might not have 뒤 과거분사로 부정절을 구성함
examples: He might not have noticed the sign.

grammar.en: Form interrogative clauses with might.
grammar.desc: might를 사용한 의문절을 구성함
examples: Might we leave a little earlier?

grammar.key: NOT ALL, NOT EVERY (not all, not every, and, and determiners)
grammar.en: Express partial negation with not all or not every.
grammar.desc: not all·not every 등으로 부분 부정을 나타냄
examples: Not every student passed the test.

grammar.key: NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE S WITHOUT NOUN ('s, of)
grammar.en: Use a possessive of-phrase with the final noun omitted.
grammar.desc: of 소유 명사구에서 앞서 언급한 끝 명사를 생략함
examples: I met one of my sister's friends and two of my brother's.

grammar.key: DESIRED STATES, WITH THERE OUGHT TO BE (ought, there ought to be)
grammar.en: Describe a desirable existence with there ought to be.
grammar.desc: there ought to be로 바람직한 존재 상태를 나타냄
examples: There ought to be more seats here.

grammar.en: Use negative present-continuous passive for ongoing acts.
grammar.desc: 현재진행 수동태 부정형으로 진행 중인 일을 나타냄
examples: The rooms are not being cleaned today.

grammar.en: Evaluate with dummy it in a passive reporting clause.
grammar.desc: 가주어 it 수동 보고절로 요약과 평가를 제시함
examples: It is generally agreed that the trial was successful.

grammar.en: Use a non-finite passive -ing clause for background.
grammar.desc: 수동 ing 비정형절로 설명 배경을 제시함
examples: Being watched so closely made her uncomfortable.

grammar.en: Order complex past events using past-simple clauses.
grammar.desc: 단순과거절로 복잡한 과거 사건의 순서를 제시함
examples: She opened the parcel, checked the contents, then called me before she left.

grammar.en: Use full negative present-perfect forms in formal contexts.
grammar.desc: 격식 맥락에서 현재완료 부정형을 축약 없이 사용함
examples: I have not received the requested documents.

grammar.en: Use a negative question to persuade.
grammar.desc: 부정 의문문으로 상대방을 설득함
examples: Don't you think we should leave now?

grammar.en: Check an opinion with a negative question.
grammar.desc: 부정 의문문으로 의견을 확인함
examples: Don't you agree that the room is too small?

grammar.en: Intensify few or many with very, too or so.
grammar.desc: very·too·so로 few·many의 수량을 강조함
examples: There are very few seats left.

grammar.en: Use pronoun none to substitute for a known quantity.
grammar.desc: 대명사 none으로 앞선 대상의 수량 부재를 나타냄
examples: They offered several options, but I chose none.

grammar.key: HYPERBOLE (millions of, loads of, tons of)
grammar.en: Use loads of or tons of for informal exaggeration.
grammar.desc: loads of·tons of 등으로 비격식 과장을 나타냄
examples: I've got tons of work to finish.

grammar.key: EITHER, NEITHER + OF + DETERMINER WITH PLURAL NOUNS (either, neither, of)
grammar.en: Use either or neither of with a plural noun phrase.
grammar.desc: either·neither of 뒤 복수 명사구를 사용함
examples: Neither of the two rooms is available.

grammar.en: Modify a relative pronoun with some of or many of.
grammar.desc: some of·many of로 관계대명사의 수량을 한정함
examples: We invited ten guests, many of whom arrived early.

grammar.en: Invert should and the subject in formal conditionals.
grammar.desc: 격식 조건절에서 should와 주어를 도치함
examples: Should the weather change, we will cancel the trip.

grammar.en: Use impersonal it with passive reporting verbs.
grammar.desc: 비인칭 it과 수동 보고동사로 정보를 제시함
examples: It is believed that the building is over a century old.

grammar.en: Introduce a subordinate condition by inverting should, had or were.
grammar.desc: should·had·were 도치로 종속 조건절을 구성함
examples: Had we arrived earlier, we would have found a seat.

grammar.en: Add question tags with there and be.
grammar.desc: there와 be를 사용한 부가의문문을 덧붙임
examples: There isn't a problem, is there?

grammar.key: SO ... AS TO, FORMAL (so, as, to)
grammar.en: Use formal so adjective as to infinitive.
grammar.desc: so 형용사 as to부정사로 격식 정도 표현을 구성함
examples: Would you be so kind as to send the file?

grammar.en: Use didn't dare with a bare infinitive for past lack of courage.
grammar.desc: didn't dare 뒤 동사 원형으로 과거의 용기 부재를 나타냄
examples: I didn't dare open the door.

grammar.en: Use that or those to signal emotional disapproval.
grammar.desc: that·those로 정서적 거리나 못마땅함을 나타냄
examples: I wish those noisy neighbours would move away.

grammar.en: Use be not plus an adjective and to-infinitive.
grammar.desc: be not 뒤 형용사와 to부정사로 부정 표현을 구성함
examples: She is not likely to arrive before noon.

grammar.en: Front not a noun phrase with passive or inversion for emphasis.
grammar.desc: not a 명사구를 문두에 놓고 수동·도치로 강조함
examples: Not a word was spoken.

grammar.en: Focus with a how, why or where cleft as subject.
grammar.desc: how·why·where 분열절을 주어로 사용하여 강조함
examples: Why she left is what I want to understand.

grammar.en: Put varied adverbs before the main verb in be going to.
grammar.desc: be going to의 본동사 앞에 다양한 부사를 사용함
examples: I am going to carefully check each detail.

grammar.en: Use have plus an object and bare infinitive for causation.
grammar.desc: have 뒤 목적어와 동사 원형으로 행동을 시킴
examples: I had the assistant print the forms.

grammar.key: DEDUCTIONS AND CONCLUSIONS (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)
grammar.en: Draw deductions with present or past have to.
grammar.desc: have to의 현재·과거형으로 추론과 결론을 나타냄
examples: The lights are on; someone has to be home.

grammar.key: LET + THIRD PERSON PRONOUN, DEVOLVING RESPONSIBILITY (let, him, her, them)
grammar.en: Use let him, her or them to assign responsibility.
grammar.desc: let him·her·them으로 책임을 넘기는 지시를 함
examples: Let them arrange the meeting themselves.

grammar.en: Use a wide range of adverbs after must.
grammar.desc: must 뒤 다양한 중간 위치 부사를 사용함
examples: You must absolutely check the date.

grammar.en: Use need in a formal rhetorical question.
grammar.desc: 격식 논의에서 need를 수사 의문문으로 사용함
examples: Need I say more?

grammar.en: Warn or reprimand with Don't you and a verb.
grammar.desc: Don't you 뒤 동사 원형으로 경고·질책함
examples: Don't you touch that button!

grammar.en: Use having been with a participle in a subordinate clause.
grammar.desc: having been과 과거분사 종속절로 배경을 나타냄
examples: Having been checked twice, the report was sent to the manager.

grammar.en: Use perfect passive -ing forms after prepositions.
grammar.desc: 전치사 뒤 완료 수동 ing형을 사용함
examples: She was pleased about having been invited.

grammar.en: Comment on an ongoing passive with have been being.
grammar.desc: have been being과 과거분사로 완료진행 수동을 나타냄
examples: The children have been being monitored closely all week.

grammar.en: Form past-perfect-continuous questions.
grammar.desc: 과거완료진행형 의문문을 구성함
examples: Had you been waiting long when I arrived?

grammar.en: Use inverted hardly had followed by when.
grammar.desc: Hardly had 도치와 when으로 직후 사건을 나타냄
examples: Hardly had we sat down when the phone rang.

grammar.en: Exclaim with How followed by an adverb and clause.
grammar.desc: How 뒤 부사와 절로 감탄문을 구성함
examples: How beautifully she sings!

grammar.en: Exclaim with How followed by a clause.
grammar.desc: How 뒤 절로 감탄문을 구성함
examples: How I wish we could stay longer!

grammar.en: Invert present perfect continuous after not only.
grammar.desc: not only 뒤 현재완료진행절을 도치하여 강조함
examples: Not only have we been waiting for an hour, but we have also missed lunch.

grammar.key: MANY ARE THE + NOUN, FOR FOCUS (many are the, many, are)
grammar.en: Use Many are the noun followed by a relative clause.
grammar.desc: Many are the 명사 뒤 관계절로 다수임을 강조함
examples: Many are the visitors who return each year.

grammar.key: A LOT AND MUCH (a lot, much)
grammar.en: Use a lot or much as the subject pronoun.
grammar.desc: a lot·much를 수량을 나타내는 주어 대명사로 사용함
examples: Much remains to be done.

grammar.en: Use each as subject and the other as object.
grammar.desc: each를 주어로 the other를 목적어로 사용함
examples: Each trusted the other.

grammar.key: WERE + PRONOUN + TO INFINITIVE, FORMAL (were, to)
grammar.en: Start a formal condition with Were subject to infinitive.
grammar.desc: Were 주어 to부정사로 격식 조건절을 구성함
examples: Were we to leave now, we could reach the station in time.

grammar.en: Use stressed will to criticize characteristic behavior.
grammar.desc: 강세를 둔 will로 반복되는 행동을 못마땅하게 나타냄
examples: He will keep interrupting me, even when I ask him to wait.

grammar.key: WITH ADVERBS (would, wouldn't, undoubtedly, possibly, normally, personally, eventually, obviously, significantly, inevitably)
grammar.en: Use a broad range of adverbs with would.
grammar.desc: would와 다양한 부사를 함께 사용함
examples: I would undoubtedly choose the quieter room.

grammar.en: Use uncontracted not in a negative question for emphasis.
grammar.desc: 부정 의문문에 축약 없는 not으로 논점을 강조함
examples: Is it not clear that we need more time?

grammar.key: INVERTED WERE + TO INFINITIVE, FORMAL (were, to)
grammar.en: Introduce formal conditions with inverted were to.
grammar.desc: were to 도치로 격식 조건절을 구성함
examples: Were she to arrive early, we could start before noon.

grammar.en: Invert a past-perfect condition before a modal-perfect result.
grammar.desc: 과거완료 조건절을 도치하고 조동사 완료 결과절을 사용함
examples: Had we booked earlier, we would have paid less.

grammar.en: Add an inverted nor clause to a negative clause.
grammar.desc: 부정절 뒤 nor 도치절로 추가 부정을 제시함
examples: She didn't call, nor did she send a message.

grammar.en: Use inverted neither or nor to add a negative factor.
grammar.desc: neither·nor 도치로 관련된 부정 요소를 추가함
examples: I don't enjoy crowds, and neither does my sister.

grammar.en: Introduce an unexpected contrast with And yet.
grammar.desc: And yet으로 예상과 다른 대조 문장을 연결함
examples: The plan looked simple. And yet it failed.

grammar.key: BE DUE TO (be due to, be, due to) (C4)
grammar.en: Use was due to for a schedule viewed from the past.
grammar.desc: was·were due to로 과거 시점의 미래 일정을 나타냄
examples: The train was due to arrive at six.
grammar.surface: BE DUE TO (be due to, be, due to)

grammar.en: Ask questions in the future perfect simple.
grammar.desc: 미래완료형 의문문을 구성함
examples: Will you have finished by Friday?

grammar.en: Use shall for a long-term intention.
grammar.desc: shall로 장기적인 의도를 나타냄
examples: We shall continue to support the school for many years.

grammar.key: OBLIGATION (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to) (C4)
grammar.en: Use have to have with a participle for a prior obligation.
grammar.desc: have to have와 과거분사로 앞서 충족할 의무를 나타냄
examples: You had to have completed the course before applying.
grammar.surface: OBLIGATION (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to)

grammar.key: PAST (have to, has to, had to, have got to, has got to, have to have)
grammar.en: Use have to have followed by a past participle.
grammar.desc: have to have 뒤 과거분사로 완료 필요 표현을 구성함
examples: You have to have finished the report by noon.

grammar.en: Add you to an imperative to strengthen an instruction.
grammar.desc: 명령문에 you를 넣어 지시를 강화함
examples: Don't you speak to her like that!

grammar.key: MAY AS WELL (may, may as well)
grammar.en: Suggest the logical option with may as well.
grammar.desc: may as well로 가장 무난하거나 논리적인 선택을 제안함
examples: We may as well take the earlier train.

grammar.key: MIGHT AS WELL (might, might as well, may)
grammar.en: Suggest an available option with might as well.
grammar.desc: might as well로 더 나은 대안이 없는 선택을 제안함
examples: We might as well wait inside.

grammar.key: INVERSION (must, mustn't, not only, never, nor)
grammar.en: Invert must after negative focus expressions.
grammar.desc: 부정 강조 표현 뒤 must와 주어를 도치함
examples: Not only must we finish today, but we must also check the results.

grammar.key: PAST, NEGATIVE (must, mustn't, must not have been, easy)
grammar.en: Use must not have been to infer a negative past state.
grammar.desc: must not have been으로 과거의 부정 상태를 추론함
examples: That journey must not have been easy.

grammar.en: Use not a plus a noun with passive for emphatic absence.
grammar.desc: not a 명사와 수동 구문으로 완전한 부재를 강조함
examples: Not a single ticket was sold.

grammar.en: Use past continuous with always for unwanted recurrence.
grammar.desc: 과거진행형과 always·constantly로 원치 않은 반복을 나타냄
examples: He was always interrupting the speaker.

grammar.key: OF THEIRS, HERS, HIS (theirs, hers, his, of)
grammar.en: Use of theirs, hers or his after a noun.
grammar.desc: 명사 뒤 of theirs·hers·his로 소유 관계를 나타냄
examples: A friend of hers is visiting.

grammar.en: Use possessive 's without a contextually known noun.
grammar.desc: 문맥상 알려진 명사를 생략하고 소유형 's만 사용함
examples: My coat is blue, but Emma's is red.

grammar.en: Use varied frequency adverbs in present continuous.
grammar.desc: 현재진행형과 다양한 빈도 부사로 반복을 강조함
examples: She is forever leaving her keys at home.

grammar.key: INVERSION WITH ONLY WHEN (only when, will)
grammar.en: Use only when with present simple and an inverted will clause.
grammar.desc: Only when 현재형 뒤 will 도치로 미래 조건을 강조함
examples: Only when she arrives will we begin.

grammar.en: Introduce a news event with present perfect.
grammar.desc: 현재완료형으로 새로운 소식을 소개함
examples: The council has opened a new library.

grammar.key: MANY A WITH SINGULAR NOUNS, FOR FOCUS (many a, many an)
grammar.en: Emphasize quantity with many a and a singular noun.
grammar.desc: many a·many an 뒤 단수 명사로 다수임을 강조함
examples: Many a visitor has admired this garden.

grammar.en: Use non-finite clauses after although or though.
grammar.desc: although·though 뒤 비정형절로 양보를 나타냄
examples: Although tired, she completed the task.

grammar.en: Give a detailed explanation with in that.
grammar.desc: in that 종속접속사로 구체적인 이유를 설명함
examples: The rooms differ in that one has a balcony.

grammar.key: SLIGHTEST, FAINTEST (slightest, faintest, the slightest, the faintest)
grammar.en: Use the slightest or faintest for minimal degree.
grammar.desc: the slightest·faintest로 최소의 정도를 나타냄
examples: I haven't the faintest idea where it is.

grammar.key: WITH AS + PRONOUN, NARRATIVE (used to, as)
grammar.en: Use as plus a pronoun and used to for narrative background.
grammar.desc: as 대명사 used to로 이야기의 과거 배경을 추가함
examples: He walked to the station, as he used to when he lived here.
